BC479.6.source: BC479 line 6: yours and your spouse's or partner's, from their return or your answer for their net income

BC479.7.label: Family income the sales tax credit allows
BC479.7.source: BC479 line 7: $18,000 with a spouse or partner on December 31, otherwise $15,000

BC479.8.label: Income for the sales tax credit

BC479.10.label: Additional sales tax credit for your spouse or common-law partner
BC479.10.source: BC479 line 10 (60350): $75 when your spouse or partner lived in British Columbia on December 31

BC479.11.label: Sales tax credits before the reduction
BC479.11.source: BC479 lines 9 (60330) to 11: $75, and $75 for your spouse or partner

BC479.13.label: Sales tax credit
BC479.13.source: BC479 lines 11 to 13: the credits less 2% of line 8, on one return of a couple

BC479.60480.label: Home renovation expenses
BC479.60480.formula: min(answer.homeAccessibility, param.bcRenovationMax, if(line.HH.partner == 1 and household.partnerInYear and person.role == "spouse" and spouse.person.province == "BC", max(0, param.bcRenovationMax - min(spouse.answer.homeAccessibility, param.bcRenovationMax)), param.bcRenovationMax))
BC479.60480.source: BC479 line 60480 and Schedule BC(S12) line 5: eligible expenses up to $10,000 for you and your spouse or partner together

BC479.14.label: Home renovation tax credit for seniors and persons with disabilities

BC479.15.label: Sales tax and home renovation credits
BC479.15.source: BC479 line 15, carried to lines 16, 35 and 36

BC479.43.label: Renter's tax credit reduction
BC479.43.source: BC479 lines 39 to 43: 2% of adjusted family net income over $64,764

BC479.44.label: British Columbia renter's tax credit
BC479.44.source: BC479 lines 38 to 44 (60576): $400 less the reduction, on one return of a couple

BC479.45.label: British Columbia credits
BC479.45.source: BC479 line 45: line 36 plus line 44, for line 47900 of your return

HH.partner.label: Spouse or common-law partner on December 31 (1 for yes)

SPOUSES.together.label: Both spouses' returns are prepared here (1 for yes)

HH.spouseNetIncome.label: Your spouse's or partner's net income
HH.spouseNetIncome.source: From their return when both returns are prepared here; otherwise from your answer

T1.10400.label: Other employment income
T1.10400.source: Employment income earned outside Canada, in Canadian dollars

T1.11500.label: Other pensions and superannuation
T1.11500.source: T4A box 016; annuities (T4A box 024) and RRIF payments (T4RIF box 16) at 65 or older, else on line 13000

T1.11600.label: Elected split-pension amount
T1.11600.source: Form T1032, line 22: the amount your spouse or partner splits with you

T1.11900.label: Employment insurance and other benefits
T1.11900.source: Box 14 of the T4E slip, and for a resident of Quebec the parental insurance benefits on the RL-6 (5005-R line 11905)

T1.11905.label: Provincial parental insurance plan (PPIP) benefits included on line 11900
T1.11905.source: 5005-R line 11905: box A of the RL-6. EI maternity and parental benefits aren't shown apart on the T4E the app reads

T1.12000.label: Taxable amount of dividends (eligible and other than eligible)
T1.12000.source: Federal Worksheet, line 12000: boxes 11 and 25 of T5 slips, boxes 32 and 50 of T3 slips

T1.12010.label: Taxable amount of dividends other than eligible

T1.12100.label: Interest and other investment income
T1.12100.source: Federal Worksheet, line 12100: box 13 of T5 slips, box 25 of T3 slips, and foreign interest and dividends

T1.12600.label: Net rental income
T1.12600.source: Form T776, line 9946 (amount 6): amount 5 less the capital cost allowance claimed

T776.9947.label: Recaptured capital cost allowance
T776.9947.source: Form T776, line 9947, and Area A, note 3: a negative column 7 is added to income

T776.5.label: Net rental income before capital cost allowance
T776.5.source: Form T776, Part 4, amounts 1 to 5: gross rents less expenses, plus recaptured capital cost allowance. A terminal loss (line 9948) isn't handled

T776A.7.label: Rental class, undepreciated capital cost after additions and dispositions
T776A.7.source: Form T776, Area A, column 7: column 2 plus column 3 minus column 5

T776A.17.label: Rental class, adjustment for 2025 additions
T776A.17.source: Form T776, Area A, column 17 and note 8: additions less the dispositions that reduce them (column 16), times 1/2

T776A.19.label: Rental class, base amount for capital cost allowance
T776A.19.source: Form T776, Area A, column 19: column 13 (column 7, with no immediate expensing) plus column 17. Column 18 is zero: no 2025 addition is under the half-year rule

T776A.20.label: Rental class, capital cost allowance rate
T776A.20.formula: if(answer.rentalCcaClass == "class1", param.ccaRateClass1, if(answer.rentalCcaClass == "class3", param.ccaRateClass3, if(answer.rentalCcaClass == "class8", param.ccaRateClass8, 0)))

T776A.21.label: Rental class, available capital cost allowance
T776A.21.source: Form T776, Area A, column 21: column 19 times column 20; none when column 7 is negative

T776.9936.label: Rental capital cost allowance claimed
T776.9936.formula: if(answer.hasRentalIncome, if(answer.rentalCcaClass == "none", 0, if(answer.rentalCcaClass == "several", unsupported("Capital cost allowance for more than one class of rental property isn't handled by this app yet"), min(line.T776A.21, max(0, line.T776.5), if(answer.rentalCcaLimit > 0, answer.rentalCcaLimit, line.T776A.21)))), 0)
T776.9936.source: Form T776, Area A, column 23, and line 9936: up to the available allowance, as much as asked, and never making or increasing a rental loss (Guide T4036, Limits on CCA)

T776A.24.label: Rental class, undepreciated capital cost at the end of the year
T776A.24.formula: if(answer.hasRentalIncome, if(answer.rentalCcaClass == "none" or answer.rentalCcaClass == "several", 0, max(0, line.T776A.7 - line.T776.9936)), 0)
T776A.24.source: Form T776, Area A, column 24: column 7 less the allowance claimed; zero after a recapture. Next year's column 2

T1.12700.label: Taxable capital gains
T1.12700.source: Schedule 3. A net capital loss isn't entered here; it carries forward

T1.12800.label: Taxable support payments received
T1.12800.source: canada.ca/taxes-support-payments: spousal support is taxable; child support under an order or agreement made after April 1997 isn't

T1.12900.label: RRSP income
T1.12900.formula: sum(T4RSP.box16) + sum(T4RSP.box18) + sum(T4RSP.box20) + sum(T4RSP.box22) + sum(T4RSP.box26) + sum(T4RSP.box28) + sum(T4RSP.box34)
T1.12900.source: T4RSP slips: every box of income. Home Buyers' Plan and Lifelong Learning Plan withdrawals (boxes 25 and 27) aren't income

T1.12905.label: Taxable FHSA income
T1.12905.source: canada.ca/line-12905: box 22 of all T4FHSA slips and box 26 for your own FHSA

T1.12906.label: Taxable FHSA income – other
T1.12906.source: canada.ca/line-12906: amounts received as the beneficiary of a deceased holder's FHSA (box 24)

T1.13000.label: Other income
T1.13000.formula: sum(T3.box26) + if(person.age < 65, sum(T4A.box024) + sum(T4RIF.box16), 0) + sum(T4A.box018) + sum(T4A.box028)
T1.13000.source: Box 26 of T3 slips; annuities and RRIF payments before 65; lump-sum payments and other income on T4A slips

T1.13010.label: Taxable scholarships, fellowships, bursaries and artists' project grants
T1.13010.formula: if(sum(T2202.box25) > 0 or (sum(T2202.box24) > 0 and answer.hasDisability), 0, if(sum(T2202.box24) > 0, max(0, sum(T4A.box105) - sum(T2202.box26) - param.scholarshipExemption), max(0, sum(T4A.box105) - param.scholarshipExemption)))
T1.13010.source: canada.ca/line-13010: not taxable for a full-time student, or a part-time student with the disability tax credit; for a part-time student, taxable above the tuition paid plus $500; otherwise above $500

SE.ownGross.label: Gross self-employment income
SE.ownGross.source: Form T2125, line 8299 (T2042 line 9659, T2121 line 8299): what was earned, with recaptured capital cost allowance

SE.own.label: Net self-employment income of your own business
SE.own.source: Form T2125, line 9946 (T2042 line 9946, T2121 line 9946): gross income less expenses and capital cost allowance

SE.flip.label: Profit on a flipped property
SE.flip.formula: if(answer.soldProperty, if(answer.propertyUse == "flipped", max(0, answer.propertyProceeds - answer.propertyCost - answer.propertyOutlays), 0), 0)
SE.flip.source: Schedule 3, Part 1, and Guide T4002, Flipped property rules: a housing unit owned less than 365 days is business income, and a loss on it is deemed nil

T1.13500.label: Net business income
T1.13500.source: Your business's net income, and the profit on a flipped property (Form T2125, Part 5 note)

T1.14100.label: Net farming income
T1.14100.formula: if(answer.hasSelfEmployment, if(answer.selfEmploymentKind == "farming", if(line.SE.own < 0, unsupported("A farming loss may be a restricted farm loss (Guide T4002), which this app doesn't handle yet"), line.SE.own), 0), 0)

SE.net.label: Net self-employment income
SE.net.source: T1 line 27, the total of lines 13500 to 14300: Schedule 8, Part 5, line 1 (with no partnership income on line 12200)

SE.earned.label: Net self-employment income, not counting losses
SE.earned.source: Schedule 6 line 3, Form T778 line 6 and Federal Worksheet line 45200: self-employment income from lines 13500 to 14300, a business's loss not counted

T2125.8230.label: Recaptured capital cost allowance
T2125.8230.formula: if(answer.hasSelfEmployment, if(answer.businessCcaClass == "none" or answer.businessCcaClass == "several" or answer.businessCcaClass == "class10_1", 0, max(0, -line.T2125A.7)), 0)
T2125.8230.source: Form T2125, Area A, note 3, line 8230 (line 9600 of T2042 and T2121): a negative column 7 is income. It doesn't apply to class 10.1

T2125A.7.label: Business class, undepreciated capital cost after additions and dispositions
T2125A.7.source: Form T2125, Area A, column 7: column 2 plus column 3 minus column 5

T2125A.17.label: Business class, adjustment for 2025 additions
T2125A.17.formula: if(answer.businessCcaClass == "class50", round(max(0, answer.businessCcaAdditions - answer.businessCcaDispositions) * 9 / 11, 2), round(max(0, answer.businessCcaAdditions - answer.businessCcaDispositions) * param.ccaRiipFactor, 2))
T2125A.17.source: Form T2125, Area A, column 17 and note 8: additions less the dispositions that reduce them (column 16), times 9/11 for class 50 and 1/2 for the others

T2125A.19.label: Business class, base amount for capital cost allowance
T2125A.19.formula: if(answer.businessCcaClass == "class10_1" and answer.businessCcaDispositions > 0, round(answer.businessUccStart * param.ccaHalfYearOnSale, 2), line.T2125A.7 + line.T2125A.17)
T2125A.19.source: Form T2125, Area A, column 19: column 13 (column 7, with no immediate expensing) plus column 17. For a class 10.1 car sold in 2025, half of column 2 (Guide T4002)

T2125A.20.label: Business class, capital cost allowance rate
T2125A.20.formula: if(answer.businessCcaClass == "class1", param.ccaRateClass1, if(answer.businessCcaClass == "class8", param.ccaRateClass8, if(answer.businessCcaClass == "class10", param.ccaRateClass10, if(answer.businessCcaClass == "class10_1", param.ccaRateClass10_1, if(answer.businessCcaClass == "class50", param.ccaRateClass50, 0)))))

T2125A.max.label: Business class, most capital cost allowance for the year
T2125A.max.source: Guide T4002, column 21: column 19 times column 20; none when column 7 is negative

T2125A.21.label: Business class, capital cost allowance for the year
T2125A.21.source: Form T2125, Area A, column 21: the most, or less if you ask for less

T2125.9936.label: Business capital cost allowance claimed
T2125.9936.formula: if(answer.hasSelfEmployment, if(answer.businessCcaClass == "none", 0, if(answer.businessCcaClass == "several", unsupported("Capital cost allowance for more than one class of business property isn't handled by this app yet"), round(line.T2125A.21 * (100 - answer.businessCcaPersonalUse) / 100, 2))), 0)
T2125.9936.source: Form T2125, line 9936: amount ii of Area A (column 21) less its personal part

T2125A.22.label: Business class, undepreciated capital cost at the end of the year
T2125A.22.formula: if(answer.hasSelfEmployment, if(answer.businessCcaClass == "none" or answer.businessCcaClass == "several" or (answer.businessCcaClass == "class10_1" and answer.businessCcaDispositions > 0), 0, max(0, line.T2125A.7 - line.T2125A.21)), 0)
T2125A.22.source: Form T2125, Area A, column 22: column 7 less column 21; zero after a recapture or once a class 10.1 car is sold. Next year's column 2

T1.14600.label: Net federal supplements paid
T1.14600.source: Box 21 of the T4A(OAS) slip: the guaranteed income supplement and allowances

T1.14700.label: Income that is deducted again on line 25000

SCOPE.departure.label: Property deemed sold when leaving Canada
SCOPE.departure.formula: if(person.residentAllYear, 0, if(answer.departureProperty, unsupported("Leaving Canada with shares, funds or other property (the deemed disposition, Forms T1243 and T1161) isn't handled by this app yet"), 0))

T1.21000.label: Deduction for elected split-pension amount
T1.21000.formula: if(answer.pensionSplit > 0 and line.HH.partner == 1 and household.partnerInYear, if(spouse.answer.pensionSplit > 0, unsupported("Only one spouse can split pension income with the other for a year. Undo one of the two splits"), min(answer.pensionSplit, line.PEN.splitMax)), 0)
T1.21000.source: Form T1032, line 22, up to the maximum on line 21

PEN.eligible.label: Eligible pension income
PEN.eligible.source: Federal Worksheet, line 31400, line 8: line 11500, and RRSP annuity payments at 65 or older

PEN.splitMax.label: Maximum split-pension amount
PEN.splitMax.source: Form T1032, lines 1 to 21: half the eligible pension income

PEN.qualifying.label: Eligible pension income other than RRIF, annuity and RRSP annuity payments
PEN.qualifying.source: Form T1032, note 1: for a receiving spouse under 65, the transferring spouse's line 1 less RRIF and annuity payments

PEN.received.label: Split-pension amount that counts for your pension income amount
PEN.received.formula: if(line.T1.11600 == 0, 0, if(line.PEN.eligible < param.pensionIncomeAmountMax and person.age < 65 and spouse.person.age >= 65 and spouse.line.PEN.qualifying < param.pensionSplitFullAnnuityBase, min(line.T1.11600, round(spouse.line.PEN.qualifying * param.pensionSplitRate, 2)), line.T1.11600))

PEN.creditBase.label: Pension income for the pension income amount
PEN.creditBase.source: Form T1032, lines 31 and 34: your eligible pension income less what you split, plus what is split with you

PEN.tax.label: Income tax deducted from eligible pension income
PEN.tax.formula: if(sum(T4A.box016) + sum(T4A.box024) + sum(T4A.box018) + sum(T4A.box028) == 0, 0, round(sum(T4A.box022) * if(person.age >= 65, sum(T4A.box016) + sum(T4A.box024), sum(T4A.box016)) / (sum(T4A.box016) + sum(T4A.box024) + sum(T4A.box018) + sum(T4A.box028)), 2)) + if(person.age >= 65, sum(T4RIF.box28), 0)
PEN.tax.source: Form T1032, line 35: the tax on the slips for eligible pension income; a T4A's tax shared in proportion to its eligible pension

PEN.taxSplit.label: Income tax deducted that goes with the split-pension amount
PEN.taxSplit.formula: if(line.T1.21000 == 0 or line.PEN.eligible == 0, 0, round(line.T1.21000 * line.PEN.tax / line.PEN.eligible, 2))

T1.21200.label: Annual union, professional, or like dues

CC.ownExpenses.label: Child care expenses entered on this return
CC.ownExpenses.source: Receipts, and the amount entered that isn't on one

CC.expenses.label: Child care expenses paid
CC.expenses.source: Form T778, line 67950 (line 5): the expenses both of you paid, when both returns are prepared here

CC.family.label: Child care is claimed in this household (1 for yes)

T778.1.label: Basic limit for children born in 2019 or later
T778.1.formula: param.childCareUnder7 * (household.childrenUnder7 - if(answer.hasChildCare, answer.childCareDisabledUnder7, if(line.SPOUSES.together == 1, if(spouse.answer.hasChildCare, spouse.answer.childCareDisabledUnder7, 0), 0)))
T778.1.source: Form T778, Part B, line 1: $8,000 for each child born in 2019 or later the disability amount can't be claimed for. The counts come from the return that entered child care

T778.2.label: Basic limit for children the disability amount can be claimed for
T778.2.formula: param.childCareDisabled * if(answer.hasChildCare, answer.childCareDisabledUnder7 + answer.childCareDisabled7to16 + answer.childCareDisabledOlder, if(line.SPOUSES.together == 1, if(spouse.answer.hasChildCare, spouse.answer.childCareDisabledUnder7 + spouse.answer.childCareDisabled7to16 + spouse.answer.childCareDisabledOlder, 0), 0))
T778.2.source: Form T778, Part B, line 2 (67960): $11,000 for each child the disability amount can be claimed for, born in 2025 or earlier

T778.3.label: Basic limit for children born from 2009 to 2018, and older infirm children
T778.3.formula: param.childCare7to16 * (household.childrenUnder17 - household.childrenUnder7 + if(answer.hasChildCare, answer.childCareInfirmOlder - answer.childCareDisabled7to16, if(line.SPOUSES.together == 1, if(spouse.answer.hasChildCare, spouse.answer.childCareInfirmOlder - spouse.answer.childCareDisabled7to16, 0), 0)))
T778.3.source: Form T778, Part B, line 3: $5,000 for each child born from 2009 to 2018, and born in 2008 or earlier with an infirmity, the disability amount can't be claimed for

CC.limit.label: Basic limit for child care expenses
CC.limit.formula: if(line.T778.1 < 0 or line.T778.3 < 0, unsupported("More children have the disability tax credit than the household's dependants born in those years. Check the counts under child care, or the people in the year"), line.T778.1 + line.T778.2 + line.T778.3)
CC.limit.source: Form T778, Part B, line 4: lines 1 to 3

CC.earned.label: Earned income
CC.earned.source: Form T778, line 6, earned income: employment income, net self-employment income (not losses), taxable scholarships and CPP disability benefits

CC.least.label: Child care you could claim
CC.least.source: Form T778, Part B, line 7: whichever is least, the basic limit, the expenses, or 2/3 of earned income

CC.netIncome.label: Net income without the child care deduction

CC.spouseNetIncome.label: Your spouse's or partner's net income without it

CC.higher.label: This return has the higher net income of the couple (1 for yes)
CC.higher.formula: if(line.HH.partner == 1, if(line.CC.netIncome > line.CC.spouseNetIncome, 1, if(line.CC.netIncome == line.CC.spouseNetIncome and household.partnerInYear and person.role == "spouse", 1, 0)), 0)
CC.higher.source: Form T778, page 1: the person with the lower net income claims. With equal incomes the couple agrees: here the person preparing claims

CC.weekly.label: Child care the higher-income spouse can claim for each week or month
CC.weekly.source: Form T778, Part C, line 10: 2.5% of line 4

CC.partC.label: Child care for the weeks and months your spouse or partner couldn't care for the children
CC.partC.source: Form T778, Part C, lines 11 to 13 (67980): line 10 times the weeks of situations b) to f), plus line 10 times the months of a)

CC.higherClaim.label: Child care claimed by the higher-income spouse
CC.higherClaim.source: Form T778, Part C, line 14: whichever is less, line 7 or line 13

T1.21400.label: Child care expenses
T1.21400.formula: if(line.CC.family == 1, if(line.CC.higher == 1, line.CC.higherClaim, max(0, line.CC.least - if(line.SPOUSES.together == 1, spouse.line.CC.higherClaim, 0))), 0)
T1.21400.source: Form T778: Part C line 14 for the higher-income spouse; otherwise Part B line 9, line 7 less what the higher-income spouse claimed (when their return isn't prepared here, taken as none). Part D, for a student claiming, isn't handled

T1.21500.label: Disability supports deduction
T1.21500.formula: if(answer.hasDisabilitySupports, min(answer.disabilitySupportsExpenses, max(0, line.T1.10100 + line.T1.10400 + line.SE.earned + line.T1.13010)), 0)
T1.21500.source: Form T929: the expenses, up to earned income (employment, self-employment and taxable scholarships)

T1.21900.label: Moving expenses
T1.21900.source: Form T1-M, line 29: net moving expenses up to the net eligible income at the new location

T1.22000.label: Deductible support payments made
T1.22000.source: canada.ca/taxes-support-payments: spousal support is deductible; child support isn't

T1.22100.label: Carrying charges, interest expenses, and other expenses

T1.22200.label: Deduction for CPP contributions on self-employment income
T1.22200.formula: if(line.CPP.employed > 0, line.T1.31000 + 2 * round(line.CPP.first * 50%, 2) + 2 * round(line.CPP.second * 50%, 2) - min(line.T1.31000 + round(line.CPP.first * 50%, 2), line.CPP.offset) - min(round(line.CPP.second * 50%, 2), max(0, line.CPP.offset - line.T1.31000 - round(line.CPP.first * 50%, 2))), line.T1.31000 + line.CPP.first + line.CPP.second)
T1.22200.source: Schedule 8, Part 4 line 17 (no employment), or Part 5 lines 70 to 88: half of each contribution, twice for the additional ones, less the employment overpayment used. In Quebec, 5005-S8 Part 3 line 15 or Part 4 lines 68 to 86, which come to the same amount (its 84.375% split of lines 73 to 75 only divides it)

T1.22215.label: Deduction for CPP enhanced contributions on employment income
T1.22215.formula: if(line.CPP.employmentDiff > 0 and line.CPP.withSelfEmployment == 0, line.CPP.requiredFirst + line.CPP.requiredSecond, line.CPP.enhancedDeduction)
T1.22215.source: Schedule 8, Part 3a line 28 (more deducted than required: the required first and second additional contributions), else Part 3b line 48 or Part 5 line 69. In Quebec, 5005-S8 Part 2a line 28, Part 2b line 47 or Part 4 line 67

T1.22300.label: Deduction for PPIP premiums on self-employment income

T1.22900.label: Other employment expenses
T1.22900.formula: if(answer.hasWorkFromHome, min(round(answer.homeOfficeExpenses * answer.homeOfficeShare / 100, 2), max(0, line.T1.10100 + line.T1.10400 - line.T1.20700 - line.T1.21200)), 0)
T1.22900.source: Form T777, lines 48 to 54: home expenses times the employment-use share, up to employment income

T1.23200.label: Other deductions
T1.23200.formula: if(answer.hasForeignIncome, max(0, answer.foreignInvestmentTax - round(answer.foreignInvestmentIncome * param.foreignPropertyTaxRate, 2)), 0) + sum(T4E.box30)
T1.23200.source: Foreign tax on foreign interest and dividends above 15% of them (Income Tax Act 20(11)), and EI benefits repaid (box 30 of the T4E)

EI.benefits.label: Regular EI benefits less the benefits repaid
EI.benefits.source: T4E repayment chart, line 0: box 15 minus box 30

EI.repayment.label: EI benefits repayment
EI.repayment.formula: if(max(0, T4E.box7) == 0, 0, if(min(T4E.box7) != 30 or max(T4E.box7) != 30 or count(T4E.box7) < count(T4E.box15), unsupported("Repaying EI benefits is worked out here only when every T4E slip with regular benefits shows 30% in box 7. Work out the chart on each T4E yourself"), round(min(line.EI.benefits, max(0, line.T1.23400 - line.T1.12500 - param.eiRepaymentThreshold)) * param.eiRepaymentRate, 2)))
EI.repayment.source: T4E repayment chart, lines 1 to 4: 30% of box 15 (less box 30) or of net income over $82,125, whichever is less, when box 7 shows 30%

T1.23500.label: Social benefits repayment
T1.23500.formula: line.EI.repayment + min(max(0, line.T1.11300 + line.T1.14600 - sum(T4AOAS.box20)), round(max(0, line.T1.23400 - line.EI.repayment - line.T1.12500 - param.oasRecoveryThreshold) * param.oasRecoveryRate, 2))
T1.23500.source: Federal Worksheet, line 23500, lines 1 to 21: the EI repayment, plus 15% of net income (less the EI repayment and RDSP income) over $93,454, up to the OAS and net federal supplements received

CPP.months.label: Months CPP or QPP applied in 2025
CPP.months.formula: if(person.province == "QC", if(person.age <= 17 or person.age >= 73, 0, if(person.age == 18, 12 - person.birthMonth, 12)), if(person.age <= 17 or person.age >= 71, 0, if(person.age == 18, 12 - person.birthMonth, if(person.age == 70, person.birthMonth, 12))))
CPP.months.source: Schedule 8, Part 2, line A: the months after the month you turned 18 (a), up to and including the month you turned 70 (f), none when 70 or older all year (g). In Quebec, 5005-S8 Part 1, line A: the months after the month you turned 18 (a), none when 73 or older at the end of 2025 (c)

CPP.ympe.label: Your maximum pensionable earnings
CPP.ympe.source: Schedule 8, Part 2, line B: $71,300 for 12 months, prorated by line A

CPP.secondMax.label: Your maximum amount subject to second additional contributions
CPP.secondMax.source: Schedule 8, Part 2, line C: $9,900 for 12 months, prorated by line A

CPP.yampe.label: Your additional maximum pensionable earnings
CPP.yampe.source: Schedule 8, Part 2, line D: $81,200 for 12 months, prorated by line A

CPP.exemption.label: Your maximum basic exemption
CPP.exemption.source: Schedule 8, Part 2, line E: $3,500 for 12 months, prorated by line A

CPP.employed.label: CPP pensionable earnings from employment
CPP.employed.formula: if(count(T4.box26) == 0, sum(T4.box14), if(count(T4.box26) >= count(T4.box14), sum(T4.box26), unsupported("Some of your T4 slips show CPP pensionable earnings (box 26) and some don't. Enter box 26 on each slip: the amount from box 14 when box 26 is blank")))
CPP.employed.source: Schedule 8, Part 3, line 1: box 26 of T4 slips (box 14 if blank)

CPP.employedSecondEarnings.label: Employment earnings subject to second additional contributions

CPP.employedBaseEarnings.label: Employment earnings subject to base and first additional contributions

CPP.deducted.label: Base and first additional CPP or QPP contributions deducted
CPP.deducted.formula: if(person.province == "QC", if(sum(T4.box16) + sum(T4.box16A) > 0, unsupported("Your T4 slips show CPP contributions (box 16 or 16A). A resident of Quebec with CPP contributions works them out on Form RC381, which this app doesn't handle yet"), sum(T4.box17)), if(sum(T4.box17) + sum(T4.box17A) > 0, unsupported("Your T4 slips show QPP contributions (box 17 or 17A). Outside Quebec, QPP contributions are worked out on Form RC381, which this app doesn't handle yet"), sum(T4.box16)))
CPP.deducted.source: Schedule 8, Part 3, line 8: box 16 of T4 slips. In Quebec, 5005-S8 Part 2, line 8: box 17. Either schedule sends a T4 with the other plan's contributions to Form RC381 (5005-S8, page 1)

CPP.secondDeducted.label: Second additional CPP or QPP contributions deducted
CPP.secondDeducted.source: Schedule 8, Part 3, line 21: box 16A of T4 slips. In Quebec, 5005-S8 Part 2, line 21: box 17A

CPP.actualBase.label: Base CPP or QPP contributions deducted
CPP.actualBase.source: Schedule 8, Part 3, lines 8 and 9: 83.1933% of box 16 of T4 slips. In Quebec, 5005-S8 Part 2, line 9: 84.375% of box 17

CPP.actualFirst.label: First additional CPP or QPP contributions deducted

CPP.requiredBase.label: Base CPP or QPP contributions required on employment earnings
CPP.requiredBase.source: Schedule 8, Part 3, line 11: 4.95%. In Quebec, 5005-S8 Part 2, line 11: 5.4%

CPP.requiredFirst.label: First additional CPP contributions required on employment earnings

CPP.firstDiff.label: First additional contributions deducted less required

CPP.baseFirstDiff.label: Base and first additional contributions deducted less required

CPP.requiredSecond.label: Second additional CPP contributions required on employment earnings

CPP.secondDiff.label: Second additional contributions deducted less required
CPP.secondDiff.source: Schedule 8, Part 3, lines 21 to 23: box 16A of T4 slips (box 17A in Quebec, 5005-S8 Part 2) less line 22

CPP.baseCredit.label: Base CPP contributions through employment, when no more was deducted than required
CPP.baseCredit.formula: if(line.CPP.baseDiff >= 0, line.CPP.requiredBase, line.CPP.actualBase + min(max(0, line.CPP.firstDiff), -line.CPP.baseDiff) + min(max(0, line.CPP.secondDiff), max(0, -line.CPP.baseDiff - max(0, line.CPP.firstDiff))))
CPP.baseCredit.source: Schedule 8, Part 3b, lines 30 to 36 (Part 5, lines 51 to 57)

CPP.enhancedDeduction.label: Enhanced CPP contributions through employment, when no more was deducted than required
CPP.enhancedDeduction.formula: if(line.CPP.firstDiff >= 0, line.CPP.requiredFirst, line.CPP.actualFirst + min(max(0, line.CPP.baseDiff), -line.CPP.firstDiff) + min(max(0, -line.CPP.firstDiff - max(0, line.CPP.baseDiff)), max(0, line.CPP.secondDiff) - min(max(0, line.CPP.secondDiff), max(0, -line.CPP.baseDiff)))) + if(line.CPP.secondDiff >= 0, line.CPP.requiredSecond, line.CPP.secondDeducted + min(max(0, line.CPP.baseFirstDiff), -line.CPP.secondDiff))
CPP.enhancedDeduction.source: Schedule 8, Part 3b, lines 37 to 48 (Part 5, lines 58 to 69); 5005-S8, Part 2b lines 36 to 47 (Part 4, lines 56 to 67)

CPP.seEarnings.label: Pensionable net self-employment earnings
CPP.seEarnings.source: Schedule 8, Part 4 line 1 and Part 5 line 1: net self-employment income, prorated by the months on line A (notes 1 and 2)

CPP.employedPaid.label: Base and first additional employment contributions, as Part 5 counts them
CPP.employedPaid.formula: line.CPP.deducted - max(0, line.CPP.baseFirstDiff) + min(max(0, line.CPP.secondDiff), max(0, -line.CPP.baseFirstDiff))
CPP.employedPaid.source: Schedule 8, Part 5, lines 5 to 10 (5005-S8, Part 4, lines 4 to 9): box 16 (17) less any overpayment, plus second additional contributions over the required that make up a shortfall

CPP.employedSecondPaid.label: Second additional employment contributions, as Part 5 counts them
CPP.employedSecondPaid.formula: line.CPP.secondDeducted - max(0, line.CPP.secondDiff) + min(max(0, line.CPP.baseFirstDiff), max(0, -line.CPP.secondDiff))
CPP.employedSecondPaid.source: Schedule 8, Part 5, lines 11 to 16 (5005-S8, Part 4, lines 10 to 15)

CPP.covered.label: Earnings already covered by employment contributions
CPP.covered.source: Schedule 8, Part 5, line 20: × 16.80672. In Quebec, 5005-S8 Part 4, line 19: × 15.625

CPP.exemptionLeft.label: Basic exemption not used by employment

CPP.baseEarnings.label: Self-employment earnings subject to base and first additional contributions
CPP.baseEarnings.formula: max(0, min(line.CPP.seEarnings, max(0, max(0, line.CPP.ympe - line.CPP.exemption) - line.CPP.covered)) - max(0, line.CPP.exemptionLeft - max(0, line.CPP.seEarnings - max(0, line.CPP.ympe - line.CPP.exemption))))
CPP.baseEarnings.source: Schedule 8, Part 5, lines 17 to 30 (Part 4, lines 3 to 9)

CPP.secondEarnings.label: Self-employment earnings subject to second additional contributions
CPP.secondEarnings.formula: if(line.CPP.seEarnings + min(line.CPP.yampe, line.CPP.employed) > line.CPP.ympe, max(0, min(line.CPP.secondMax - round(line.CPP.employedSecondPaid / param.cpp2EmployeeRate, 2), line.CPP.seEarnings - line.CPP.exemptionLeft - line.CPP.baseEarnings)), 0)
CPP.secondEarnings.source: Schedule 8, Part 5, lines 31 to 42 (Part 4, lines 4 to 6)

CPP.base.label: Base CPP or QPP contributions on self-employment earnings
CPP.base.source: Schedule 8, Part 5, line 43: 9.9%. In Quebec, 5005-S8 Part 3 line 10 and Part 4 line 42: 10.8%

CPP.first.label: First additional CPP contributions on self-employment earnings

CPP.second.label: Second additional CPP contributions on self-employment earnings

CPP.withSelfEmployment.label: Part 5 applies (1 for yes)
CPP.withSelfEmployment.source: Schedule 8, Part 3 and Part 5, note after line 42

CPP.offset.label: Employment contributions deducted over the required, used against self-employment contributions
CPP.offset.source: Schedule 8, Part 5, lines 48 and 73: line 24 of Part 3, if positive

T1.24400.label: Canadian Armed Forces personnel and police deduction

T1.25000.label: Other payments deduction
T1.25000.formula: if(line.T1.14600 > 0 and max(0, line.T1.23400) - line.T1.12500 > param.oasRecoveryThreshold, unsupported("Net federal supplements with net income over $93,454 (line 25000) aren't handled by this app yet"), line.T1.14700)
T1.25000.source: Federal Worksheet, line 25000: the amount on line 14700

T1.25300.label: Net capital losses of other years
T1.25300.source: canada.ca/line-25300: up to the taxable capital gains of the year

NRD.days.label: Days you lived in a northern zone in 2025
NRD.days.formula: if(person.province == "YT" or person.province == "NT" or person.province == "NU", if(answer.hasNorthernResidence, min(param.northernDaysMax, answer.northernDays), 0), 0)

NRD.shared.label: Both spouses lived in a northern zone (1 for yes)
NRD.shared.formula: if(line.HH.partner == 1 and household.partnerInYear, if(line.NRD.days > 0 and spouse.line.NRD.days > 0, 1, 0), 0)

NRD.first.label: This return is the one that would claim both amounts (1 for yes)
NRD.first.formula: if(line.T1.23600 > spouse.line.T1.23600 or (line.T1.23600 == spouse.line.T1.23600 and person.role == "self"), 1, 0)

NRD.basic.label: Residency deduction claiming the basic amount only

NRD.oneClaims.label: One spouse claims both amounts for the home (1 for yes)
NRD.oneClaims.formula: if(line.NRD.first == 1, if(line.NRD.both >= line.NRD.basic + spouse.line.NRD.basic, 1, 0), if(spouse.line.NRD.both >= spouse.line.NRD.basic + line.NRD.basic, 1, 0))

T2222.1.label: Basic residency amount
T2222.1.formula: if(line.NRD.days == 0, 0, if(line.NRD.shared == 1, if(line.NRD.oneClaims == 1 and line.NRD.first == 0, 0, line.NRD.days * param.northernBasicPerDay), line.NRD.days * param.northernBasicPerDay))
T2222.1.source: Form T2222, Step 2, line 1: $11 for each day

T2222.2.label: Additional residency amount
T2222.2.formula: if(line.NRD.days == 0, 0, if(line.NRD.shared == 1, if(line.NRD.oneClaims == 1 and line.NRD.first == 1, line.NRD.days * param.northernAdditionalPerDay, 0), if(answer.northernHome == "alone", line.NRD.days * param.northernAdditionalPerDay, 0)))
T2222.2.source: Form T2222, Step 2, line 2: $11 for each day, when no one else in the home claims the basic amount

T2222.12.label: Most residency deduction
T2222.12.source: Form T2222, Step 2, line 12: 20% of net income

T1.25500.label: Northern residents deductions
T1.25500.source: Form T2222, lines 13 and 19: the residency deduction; no travel deduction

RES.days.label: Days you lived in Canada in 2025

RES.full.label: Full personal amounts while not resident (1 for yes)
RES.full.formula: if(person.residentAllYear, 1, if(answer.nonResidentIncome == 0 or answer.nonResidentCanadianIncome >= round(answer.nonResidentIncome * param.nonResidentCanadaShare, 2), 1, 0))
RES.full.source: canada.ca, newcomers and emigrants: the full amounts when Canadian income was 90% or more of world income for the part of the year not resident

RES.factor.label: Share of the personal amounts you can claim
RES.factor.source: 1 for the full amounts; otherwise the days in Canada over 365. Both are read, so both questions are asked

FULL.30000.label: Basic personal amount for a full year
FULL.30000.formula: round(param.basicPersonalAmountMax - (param.basicPersonalAmountMax - param.basicPersonalAmountMin) * clamp(line.T1.23600 - param.basicPersonalAmountPhaseStart, 0, param.basicPersonalAmountPhaseEnd - param.basicPersonalAmountPhaseStart) / (param.basicPersonalAmountPhaseEnd - param.basicPersonalAmountPhaseStart), 2)
FULL.30000.source: Federal Worksheet, line 30000: the full amount up to the 26% bracket, going down to the minimum at the 33% bracket

T1.30000.label: Basic personal amount
T1.30000.source: Federal Worksheet, line 30000: the full amount up to the 26% bracket, going down to the minimum at the 33% bracket

T1.30100.label: Age amount
T1.30100.formula: round((if(person.age >= 65, max(0, param.ageAmountMax - round(max(0, line.T1.23600 - param.ageAmountThreshold) * param.ageAmountRate, 2)), 0)) * line.RES.factor, 2)
T1.30100.source: Federal Worksheet, line 30100: for people born in 1960 or earlier

FULL.30300.label: Spouse or common-law partner amount for a full year
FULL.30300.formula: if(line.HH.partner == 1, max(0, line.FULL.30000 + if(answer.spouseInfirm, param.caregiverChildAmount, 0) - line.HH.spouseNetIncome), 0)

T1.30300.label: Spouse or common-law partner amount
T1.30300.source: Schedule 5 line 30300: your basic personal amount (plus $2,687 for a spouse with an infirmity) minus their net income

T1.30400.label: Amount for an eligible dependant
T1.30400.source: Schedule 5 line 30400: for a single parent, one child under 18 who lived with you. The app assumes the child had no income

T1.30425.label: Canada caregiver amount for spouse or common-law partner
T1.30425.formula: round((if(line.HH.partner == 1 and answer.spouseInfirm, max(0, min(param.caregiverMax, max(0, param.caregiverBase - line.HH.spouseNetIncome)) - line.FULL.30300), 0)) * line.RES.factor, 2)
T1.30425.source: Schedule 5 line 30425: $28,798 less their net income (up to $8,601), less the spouse amount

T1.30450.label: Canada caregiver amount for other infirm dependants age 18 or older
T1.30450.formula: round((if(answer.hasInfirmDependant, if(answer.infirmDependants > 1, unsupported("The Canada caregiver amount for more than one adult dependant isn't handled by this app yet"), if(answer.infirmDependants == 0, 0, min(param.caregiverMax, max(0, param.caregiverBase - answer.infirmDependantIncome)))), 0)) * line.RES.factor, 2)
T1.30450.source: Schedule 5 line 30450: $28,798 less the dependant's net income, up to $8,601

T1.30500.label: Canada caregiver amount for infirm children under 18 years of age
T1.30500.source: T1 lines 30499 and 30500: $2,687 for each child

T1.T84.label: Credit amounts for you and your dependants (T1 line 84)

T1.30800.label: Base CPP contributions through employment
T1.30800.source: Schedule 8, Part 3a line 25 (more deducted than required: the required base contributions), else Part 3b line 36 or Part 5 line 57. In Quebec, 5005-S8 Part 2a line 25, Part 2b line 35 or Part 4 line 55

T1.31000.label: CPP contributions on self-employment income
T1.31000.source: Schedule 8, Part 4 line 15 or Part 5 line 70: half the base contributions. In Quebec, 5005-S8 Part 3 line 14 or Part 4 line 68

EI.insurable.label: EI insurable earnings
EI.insurable.formula: if(count(T4.box24) == 0, sum(T4.box14), if(count(T4.box24) >= count(T4.box14), sum(T4.box24), unsupported("Some of your T4 slips show EI insurable earnings (box 24) and some don't. Enter box 24 on each slip: the amount from box 14 when box 24 is blank")))
EI.insurable.source: Form T2204, line 1: box 24 of T4 slips (box 14 if blank)

EI.required.label: EI premiums required
EI.required.formula: if(person.province == "QC", if(line.EI.insurable <= param.eiMinInsurableEarnings, 0, min(param.eiPremiumMaxQc, round(line.EI.insurable * param.eiPremiumRateQc, 2))), if(line.EI.insurable < param.eiMinInsurableEarnings, 0, min(param.eiPremiumMax, round(line.EI.insurable * param.eiPremiumRate, 2))))
EI.required.source: Form T2204, lines 10 and 12: 1.64% of line 1, up to $1,077.48; line 1 is 0 when insurable earnings are less than $2,000 (note 1). In Quebec, 5005-S10 Part C, lines 18 to 20: 1.31%, up to $860.67; line 18 is 0 when insurable earnings are $2,000 or less

T1.31200.label: Employment insurance premiums through employment
T1.31200.formula: if(person.province == "QC", min(line.EI.required, sum(T4.box18)), min(max(0, min(param.eiMaxInsurableEarnings, line.EI.insurable) - param.eiMinInsurableEarnings), sum(T4.box18), line.EI.required))
T1.31200.source: Form T2204, line 16: whichever is least of insurable earnings (up to $65,700) over $2,000, the premiums deducted (box 18), and the premiums required. In Quebec, 5005-S10 Part C, line 24: whichever is less, line 20 or the premiums deducted (box 18)

PPIP.insurable.label: PPIP insurable earnings
PPIP.insurable.formula: if(person.province == "QC", if(count(T4.box56) == 0, sum(T4.box14), if(count(T4.box56) >= count(T4.box14), sum(T4.box56), unsupported("Some of your T4 slips show PPIP insurable earnings (box 56) and some don't. Enter box 56 on each slip: the amount from box 14 when box 56 is blank"))), 0)
PPIP.insurable.source: 5005-S10, Part A line 3 and Part B line 13: box 56 of T4 slips (box 14 if blank)

T1.31205.label: PPIP premiums paid
T1.31205.formula: if(person.province == "QC", if(line.PPIP.insurable < param.ppipMinEarnings, 0, min(param.ppipPremiumMax, sum(T4.box55))), if(sum(T4.box55) > 0, unsupported("PPIP premiums (box 55 of a T4) of a person living outside Quebec on December 31 aren't handled by this app yet"), 0))
T1.31205.source: 5005-R line 31205 and canada.ca/line-31205: box 55 of all T4 slips, up to $484.12; nothing when PPIP insurable earnings are less than $2,000 (the TP-1 refunds them)

PPIP.seEarnings.label: Self-employment income subject to the PPIP premium
PPIP.seEarnings.formula: if(person.province == "QC" and max(0, line.SE.net) + line.PPIP.insurable >= param.ppipMinEarnings, min(max(0, line.SE.net), max(0, param.ppipMaxInsurableEarnings - line.PPIP.insurable)), 0)
PPIP.seEarnings.source: 5005-S10, Part A, lines 1 to 5: net business income (TP-1 Schedule L line 27, the self-employment lines here, not less than 0), up to $98,000 less the PPIP insurable employment earnings; none when the two total less than $2,000 (TP-1 Schedule R)

T1.31215.label: PPIP premiums payable on self-employment income
T1.31215.source: 5005-S10, Part A, line 10: line 7 minus line 9 (maximum $484.12)

T1.31240.label: Search and rescue volunteers' amount
T1.31240.source: T1 lines 31220 and 31240: one or the other

T1.31270.label: Home buyers' amount
T1.31270.formula: if(household.partnerInYear and line.HH.partner == 1 and answer.homeBuyers + spouse.answer.homeBuyers > param.homeBuyersMax, unsupported("You and your spouse or partner can claim at most $10,000 together for the home buyers' amount. Lower one of the claims"), min(answer.homeBuyers, param.homeBuyersMax))

T1.31300.label: Adoption expenses
T1.31300.formula: if(answer.hasAdoption, if(answer.adoptedChildren > 1 and answer.adoptionExpenses > param.adoptionMax, unsupported("Adoption expenses over $19,580 for more than one child are claimed child by child, which this app doesn't handle yet"), min(answer.adoptionExpenses, param.adoptionMax)), 0)
T1.31300.source: canada.ca/line-31300: up to $19,580 for each child

T1.T96.label: CPP, EI, PPIP, volunteer, employment, home and adoption amounts (T1 line 96; line 100 of 5005-R)

T1.31400.label: Pension income amount
T1.31400.source: Federal Worksheet, line 31400, and Form T1032 when splitting: eligible pension income, up to $2,000

T1.31600.label: Disability amount for self
T1.31600.source: T1 line 31600: $10,138 at 18 or older, with an approved Form T2201

T1.31800.label: Disability amount transferred from a dependant
T1.31800.formula: round((if(answer.hasDisabledDependant, if(answer.disabledChildren > 1 and answer.disabledChildCare > 0, unsupported("Child care for more than one child with a disability is worked out child by child, which this app doesn't handle yet"), answer.disabledChildren * (param.disabilityAmount + param.disabilitySupplementMax) - min(answer.disabledChildren * param.disabilitySupplementMax, max(0, answer.disabledChildCare - param.disabilityCareThreshold)) + answer.disabledAdults * param.disabilityAmount), 0)) * line.RES.factor, 2)
T1.31800.source: Federal Worksheet, line 31800: $10,138, plus up to $5,914 for a child under 18, less care over $3,464. The app assumes the dependant had no income

T1.31900.label: Interest paid on your student loans

T1.32400.label: Tuition amount transferred from a child or grandchild

CHILD.provincialTuition.label: Provincial or territorial tuition transferred from a child or grandchild
CHILD.provincialTuition.source: The amount on the student's T2202 for your province or territory, asked once a federal amount is transferred

T1.32600.label: Amounts transferred from your spouse or common-law partner
T1.32600.source: Schedule 2: their unused age amount and the tuition they designate to you

T1.33099.label: Medical expenses for you, your spouse and your children
T1.33099.formula: if(household.partnerInYear and spouse.answer.claimSpouseMedical and line.HH.partner == 1, 0, line.OWN.medical) + if(household.partnerInYear and answer.claimSpouseMedical and line.HH.partner == 1, spouse.line.OWN.medical, 0)
T1.33099.source: Either spouse can claim the family's medical expenses: this return's own, unless the spouse claims them, and the spouse's when this return claims them

OWN.medical.label: Medical expenses on this return's receipts and entered here
OWN.medical.source: Medical expense receipts, and the amount entered that isn't on one

T1.33199.label: Allowable amount of medical expenses for other dependants
T1.33199.formula: if(answer.hasOtherDependantMedical, max(0, answer.otherDependantMedical - min(param.medicalThresholdMax, round(answer.otherDependantIncome * param.medicalThresholdRate, 2))), 0)
T1.33199.source: Federal Worksheet, line 33199: their expenses over whichever is less, $2,834 or 3% of their net income

T1.33200.label: Allowable medical expenses
T1.33200.formula: max(0, line.T1.33099 - min(param.medicalThresholdMax, round(line.T1.23600 * param.medicalThresholdRate, 2))) + line.T1.33199
T1.33200.source: T1 lines 107 to 112: expenses over whichever is less, $2,834 or 3% of net income, and those for other dependants

T1.33800.label: Credit amounts at the credit rate

T1.34990.label: Top-up tax credit
T1.34990.source: Federal Worksheet, line 34990: keeps credit amounts above the first bracket at 15%

T1.40425.label: Federal dividend tax credit
T1.40425.source: Federal Worksheet, line 40425: the credit as shown on the slips

FTC.netForeign.label: Net foreign non-business income
FTC.netForeign.source: Form T2209, note 2: the foreign income less the foreign tax deducted under 20(11) (line 23200, without the EI benefits repaid)

FTC.eligibleTax.label: Non-business income tax paid to a foreign country
FTC.eligibleTax.source: Form T2209, line 1: foreign tax on interest and dividends counts up to 15% of them

FTC.basicFederalTax.label: Basic federal tax, for the foreign tax credit
FTC.basicFederalTax.source: Form T2209, note 4: line 42900 plus the federal dividend tax credit

T1.40500.label: Federal foreign tax credit
T1.40500.formula: if(line.FTC.eligibleTax > 0 and line.T1.23600 > 0, min(line.FTC.eligibleTax, round(min(line.FTC.netForeign, line.T1.23600) * line.FTC.basicFederalTax / line.T1.23600, 2), line.T1.42900), 0)
T1.40500.source: Form T2209, line 3: the foreign tax, up to the share of basic federal tax on the foreign income

FTC.left.label: Foreign tax left for the provincial credit

T1.41600.label: Federal political contribution, investment and labour-sponsored funds credits

T1.42800.label: Provincial tax
T1.42800.formula: if(person.province == "ON", line.ON428.90, if(person.province == "BC", line.BC428.91, if(person.province == "AB", line.AB428.75, if(person.province == "MB", line.MB428.82, if(person.province == "SK", line.SK428.82, if(person.province == "NB", line.NB428.97, if(person.province == "NL", line.NL428.105, if(person.province == "NS", line.NS428.99, if(person.province == "PE", line.PE428.97, if(person.province == "YT", line.YT428.79, if(person.province == "NT", line.NT428.66, if(person.province == "NU", line.NU428.66, if(person.province == "QC", 0, unsupported("Provincial tax for this province isn't handled by this app"))))))))))))))
T1.42800.source: The Form 428 of your province or territory. A resident of Quebec has none: Quebec's tax is on the TP-1, and 5005-R line 42800 is only for Form T2203 (a business with a permanent establishment outside Quebec), which isn't handled

T1.42100.label: CPP contributions payable on self-employment income
T1.42100.formula: if(person.province == "QC", 0, max(0, line.CPP.base + line.CPP.first + line.CPP.second - 2 * line.CPP.offset))
T1.42100.source: Schedule 8, Part 4 line 14, or Part 5 line 49 when positive: the contributions less twice the employment overpayment. 5005-R has no line 42100: a resident of Quebec pays QPP on self-employment on the TP-1 (line 445, Schedule U)

T1.43700.label: Total income tax deducted
T1.43700.formula: sum(T4.box22) + sum(T4A.box022) + sum(T4AP.box22) + sum(T4AOAS.box22) + sum(T4E.box22) + sum(T4RIF.box28) + sum(T4RSP.box30) + sum(T4FHSA.box30) - line.PEN.taxSplit + if(line.HH.partner == 1 and household.partnerInYear, spouse.line.PEN.taxSplit, 0)
T1.43700.source: The income tax deducted on all slips; with pension splitting, the tax that goes with the split (Form T1032, lines 39 and 42)

T1.44800.label: CPP overpayment
T1.44800.formula: if(person.province == "QC", 0, if(line.CPP.withSelfEmployment == 1, round(max(0, 2 * line.CPP.offset - line.CPP.base - line.CPP.first - line.CPP.second) * 50%, 2), max(0, line.CPP.employmentDiff)))
T1.44800.source: Schedule 8, Part 3a line 29 (line 24 when positive), or Part 5 line 50: half of line 49 when negative. 5005-R has no line 44800: a resident of Quebec claims a QPP overpayment on the TP-1 (line 452; 5005-S8 Part 2a and Part 4 note 1)

T1.45000.label: Employment insurance overpayment
T1.45000.formula: if(person.province == "QC", max(0, sum(T4.box18) - line.T1.31200), if(sum(T4.box18) - line.T1.31200 > 1, sum(T4.box18) - line.T1.31200, 0))
T1.45000.source: Form T2204, lines 8 to 15: the premiums deducted less line 16, when more than $1. In Quebec, 5005-S10 Part C, line 23: box 18 less line 20, if positive

T1.45100.label: Net EI overpayment
T1.45100.source: 5005-R lines 157 to 159: line 45000 less line 31210 (not claimed here: the app doesn't keep a T4's province of employment). Only on the T1 for residents of Quebec

T1.44000.label: Refundable Quebec abatement
T1.44000.source: 5005-R line 44000 (row 156) and canada.ca/line-44000: line 42900 × 16.5%, for a resident of Quebec on December 31. Form T2203 (a business with a permanent establishment outside Quebec) isn't handled

MED.earned.label: Earnings for the refundable medical expense supplement
MED.earned.formula: max(0, line.T1.10100 + line.T1.10400 - line.T1.20700 - line.T1.21200 - line.T1.22900) + line.SE.earned
MED.earned.source: Federal Worksheet, line 45200: employment income less lines 20700, 21200 and 22900, and net self-employment income

MED.familyIncome.label: Adjusted family net income for the refundable medical expense supplement
MED.familyIncome.formula: max(0, line.T1.23600 - line.T1.12500) + if(line.HH.partner == 1, if(household.partnerInYear, max(0, spouse.line.T1.23600 - spouse.line.T1.12500), line.HH.spouseNetIncome), 0)

T1.45200.label: Refundable medical expense supplement
T1.45200.formula: if(person.residentAllYear and person.age >= 18 and line.MED.earned >= param.medicalSupplementMinEarnings, max(0, min(round((line.T1.21500 + line.T1.33200) * param.medicalSupplementRate, 2), param.medicalSupplementMax) - round(max(0, line.MED.familyIncome - param.medicalSupplementThreshold) * param.medicalSupplementReductionRate, 2)), 0)
T1.45200.source: Federal Worksheet, line 45200: 25% of lines 21500 and 33200, up to $1,504, less 5% of family net income over $33,294

CWB.netIncome.label: Net income for the Canada workers benefit

CWB.dependant.label: An eligible dependant (1 for yes)
CWB.dependant.source: Schedule 6: a child under 19 who lived with you on December 31

CWB.student.label: A full-time student for more than 13 weeks without an eligible dependant (1 for yes)

CWB.eligible.label: Eligible for the Canada workers benefit (1 for yes)
CWB.eligible.formula: if(person.residentAllYear and line.CWB.student == 0 and (person.age >= 19 or line.CWB.spouse == 1 or line.CWB.dependant == 1), 1, 0)
CWB.eligible.source: Schedule 6: resident in Canada all year, 19 or older (or with a spouse or a child) and not a full-time student for more than 13 weeks

CWB.familyIncome.label: Adjusted family net income
CWB.familyIncome.formula: if(line.CWB.spouse == 1, if(household.partnerInYear, line.CWB.netIncome + spouse.line.CWB.netIncome - min(param.cwbSecondaryEarnerMax, if(line.CWB.working < spouse.line.CWB.working, min(line.CWB.working, line.CWB.netIncome), min(spouse.line.CWB.working, spouse.line.CWB.netIncome))), if(line.CWB.netIncome + line.HH.spouseNetIncome - min(param.cwbSecondaryEarnerMax, line.CWB.netIncome, line.HH.spouseNetIncome) < line.CWB.familyLimit and line.CWB.working > 0, unsupported("The Canada workers benefit for a couple needs your spouse's or partner's working income: prepare their return here too"), line.CWB.familyLimit)), line.CWB.netIncome)
CWB.familyIncome.source: Schedule 6, lines 13 to 15: with the secondary earner exemption (up to $16,386). With a spouse whose return isn't prepared here, a family that might get the benefit is asked to prepare it; one that can't is put at the limit

CWB.familyLimit.label: Adjusted family net income from which a family gets no Canada workers benefit
CWB.familyLimit.source: Schedule 6 (5005-S6 in Quebec), the chart of limits: the highest limit

CWB.workingBase.label: Working income where the basic benefit starts
CWB.workingBase.source: Schedule 6, line 17: $3,000. In Quebec, 5005-S6 line 17: $3,600 with an eligible spouse, else $2,400

CWB.rate.label: Basic benefit rate on working income
CWB.rate.formula: if(person.province == "QC", if(line.CWB.dependant == 1, if(line.CWB.spouse == 1, param.cwbQcRateSpouseDependant, param.cwbQcRateDependant), param.cwbQcRate), param.cwbRate)
CWB.rate.source: Schedule 6, line 19: 27%. In Quebec, 5005-S6 line 19: 20% with an eligible dependant and no eligible spouse, 23.9% with both, else 37.3%

CWB.max.label: Most basic Canada workers benefit
CWB.max.formula: if(person.province == "QC", if(line.CWB.spouse == 1, if(line.CWB.dependant == 1, param.cwbQcMaxSpouseDependant, param.cwbQcMaxSpouse), if(line.CWB.dependant == 1, param.cwbQcMaxDependant, param.cwbQcMaxSingle)), if(line.CWB.spouse == 1 or line.CWB.dependant == 1, param.cwbMaxFamily, param.cwbMaxSingle))
CWB.max.source: Schedule 6, line 21 (5005-S6 line 21 in Quebec, by family type)

CWB.incomeBase.label: Adjusted family net income where the basic benefit starts to go down
CWB.incomeBase.formula: if(person.province == "QC", if(line.CWB.spouse == 1, if(line.CWB.dependant == 1, param.cwbQcIncomeBaseSpouseDependant, param.cwbQcIncomeBaseSpouse), if(line.CWB.dependant == 1, param.cwbQcIncomeBaseDependant, param.cwbQcIncomeBaseSingle)), if(line.CWB.spouse == 1 or line.CWB.dependant == 1, param.cwbIncomeBaseFamily, param.cwbIncomeBaseSingle))
CWB.incomeBase.source: Schedule 6, line 24 (5005-S6 line 24 in Quebec, by family type)

CWB.disabilityWorkingBase.label: Working income where the disability supplement starts

CWB.disabilityRate.label: Disability supplement rate on working income
CWB.disabilityRate.source: Schedule 6, line 32: 27%. In Quebec, 5005-S6 line 32: 20% with an eligible spouse, else 40%

CWB.disabilityMax.label: Most Canada workers benefit disability supplement

CWB.disabilityIncomeBase.label: Adjusted family net income where the disability supplement starts to go down
CWB.disabilityIncomeBase.formula: if(person.province == "QC", if(line.CWB.spouse == 1, if(line.CWB.dependant == 1, param.cwbQcDisabilityIncomeBaseSpouseDependant, param.cwbQcDisabilityIncomeBaseSpouse), if(line.CWB.dependant == 1, param.cwbQcDisabilityIncomeBaseDependant, param.cwbQcDisabilityIncomeBaseSingle)), if(line.CWB.spouse == 1 or line.CWB.dependant == 1, param.cwbDisabilityIncomeBaseFamily, param.cwbDisabilityIncomeBaseSingle))
CWB.disabilityIncomeBase.source: Schedule 6, line 36 (5005-S6 line 36 in Quebec, by family type)

CWB.disabilityReductionRate.label: Disability supplement reduction rate
CWB.disabilityReductionRate.formula: if(line.CWB.spouse == 1 and household.partnerInYear and spouse.answer.hasDisability, if(person.province == "QC", param.cwbQcReductionRateBothDisabled, param.cwbReductionRateBothDisabled), if(person.province == "QC", param.cwbQcReductionRate, param.cwbReductionRate))
CWB.disabilityReductionRate.source: Schedule 6, line 38: 15% (7.5% when both spouses have the disability tax credit). In Quebec, 5005-S6 line 38: 20% (10%)

CWB.claimsBasic.label: This return claims the couple's basic benefit (1 for yes)
CWB.claimsBasic.formula: if(line.CWB.eligible == 0, 0, if(line.CWB.spouse == 0 or not household.partnerInYear, 1, if(spouse.line.CWB.eligible == 0 or line.CWB.working > spouse.line.CWB.working or (line.CWB.working == spouse.line.CWB.working and person.role == "self"), 1, 0)))

CWB.basic.label: Basic Canada workers benefit
CWB.basic.formula: if(line.CWB.claimsBasic == 1, max(0, min(round(max(0, line.CWB.familyWorking - line.CWB.workingBase) * line.CWB.rate, 2), line.CWB.max) - round(max(0, line.CWB.familyIncome - line.CWB.incomeBase) * line.CWB.reductionRate, 2)), 0)
CWB.basic.source: Schedule 6, Step 2, lines 16 to 28: 27% of family working income over $3,000, up to the maximum, less 15% of adjusted family net income over the base (in Quebec, 5005-S6 Step 2 with its own amounts and rates)

CWB.disability.label: Canada workers benefit disability supplement
CWB.disability.formula: if(line.CWB.eligible == 1 and answer.hasDisability, max(0, min(round(max(0, line.CWB.working - line.CWB.disabilityWorkingBase) * line.CWB.disabilityRate, 2), line.CWB.disabilityMax) - round(max(0, line.CWB.familyIncome - line.CWB.disabilityIncomeBase) * line.CWB.disabilityReductionRate, 2)), 0)
CWB.disability.source: Schedule 6, Step 3, lines 29 to 40: 27% of working income over $1,150, up to $843, less 15% (7.5% when both spouses have the disability tax credit) of adjusted family net income over the base (in Quebec, 5005-S6 Step 3 with its own amounts and rates)

T1.41500.label: Advanced Canada workers benefit
T1.41500.formula: min(max(line.CWB.basic, line.T1.45300), if(line.CWB.claimsBasic == 1, sum(RC210.box10) + if(household.partnerInYear and line.HH.partner == 1, sum(spouse.RC210.box10), 0), 0) + sum(RC210.box11))
T1.41500.source: Schedule 6, Step 4: the advance payments (RC210 box 10 of both spouses, on the return claiming the basic benefit, and box 11), up to the benefit

T1.45350.label: Canada training credit
T1.45350.source: Schedule 11, lines 1 to 5: for a resident of Canada all year

T1.45355.label: Multigenerational home renovation tax credit
T1.45355.source: Schedule 12: 14.5% of qualifying expenditures, up to $50,000

T1.46900.label: Eligible educator school supply tax credit

T1.47900.label: Provincial or territorial credits
T1.47900.formula: if(person.province == "ON", line.ON479.21, if(person.province == "BC", line.BC479.45, if(person.province == "NB", line.NBS12.7, if(person.province == "MB", line.MB479.81, if(person.province == "SK", line.SK479.10, if(person.province == "NL", line.NL479.9, if(person.province == "NS", line.NS479.5, if(person.province == "PE", line.PE428.98, if(person.province == "YT", line.YT479.6, if(person.province == "NT", line.NT479.21, if(person.province == "NU", line.NU479.21, 0)))))))))))
T1.47900.source: T1 line 47900: the Form 479 of your province or territory. 5005-R (Quebec) has no line 47900 and there is no Form 479 for Quebec: Quebec's credits are on the TP-1

T1.48200.label: Total credits
T1.48200.formula: line.T1.43700 + line.T1.45200 + line.T1.45300 + line.T1.45350 + line.T1.45355 + line.T1.45600 + line.T1.46900 + line.T1.47600 + if(person.province == "QC", line.T1.44000 + line.T1.45100, line.T1.44800 + line.T1.45000 + line.T1.47900)
T1.48200.source: T1 line 48200 (row 166). In Quebec, 5005-R row 171: lines 155 (43850, which is line 43700: the tax transfer on line 43800 isn't handled), 156 (44000) and 159 to 170, with no line 44800 or 47900

S2.6.label: Their age amount, pension income amount, and the tuition they designate to you

S2.7.label: Their taxable income, for the transfer

S2.11.label: Their basic personal amount, CPP, EI and employment amounts, and tuition
S2.11.source: Schedule 2 lines 8 to 11: their lines 30000, 96 and 32300

S2.13.label: Federal amounts transferred from your spouse or common-law partner

S3.13200.label: Gain or loss on publicly traded shares and mutual fund units
S3.13200.source: Schedule 3 line 4: proceeds (T5008 box 20) minus cost (box 21)

S3.13800.label: Gain or loss on real estate
S3.13800.source: Schedule 3 line 5: proceeds less the adjusted cost base and selling costs. A home that was your principal residence every year has no gain (Form T2091)

S3.15800.label: Gain on personal-use property
S3.15800.formula: if(answer.soldProperty, if(answer.propertyUse == "personal_use", max(0, answer.propertyProceeds - answer.propertyCost - answer.propertyOutlays), 0), 0) + line.T2091.24
S3.15800.source: Schedule 3 line 8: a cottage or other property for your own use (a loss on it isn't allowed), and the gain on a home that was your principal residence only some of the years (Form T2091(IND), Part 4)

S3.17900.label: Principal residence designation (the box to tick)
S3.17900.source: Schedule 3, Part 2, line 17900: box 1 for every year owned (or all but one), box 2 for some of the years. A home sold is designated on Form T2091(IND) even when its whole gain is exempt

T2091.18.label: Capital gain on the home before the principal residence exemption
T2091.18.source: Form T2091(IND), lines 14 to 18: proceeds less the adjusted cost base and the selling costs

T2091.23.label: Principal residence exemption
T2091.23.formula: if(line.T2091.18 > 0, if(answer.propertyYearsOwned < 1 or answer.propertyYearsDesignated > answer.propertyYearsOwned, unsupported("The years you designate the home as your principal residence can't be more than the years you owned it, and you owned it at least one year (Form T2091(IND), lines 3 and 7)"), min(line.T2091.18, round(line.T2091.18 * (answer.propertyYearsDesignated + 1) / answer.propertyYearsOwned, 2))), 0)
T2091.23.source: Form T2091(IND), lines 19 to 23: the gain times (the years designated plus 1) divided by the years owned

T2091.24.label: Capital gain on the home after the exemption
T2091.24.source: Form T2091(IND), line 24, carried to line 54 and to line 15800 of Schedule 3

S3.19900.label: Taxable capital gains or net capital loss

S9.5.label: Total eligible amount of charitable donations
S9.5.formula: if(household.partnerInYear and spouse.answer.claimSpouseDonations and line.HH.partner == 1, 0, line.OWN.donations) + if(household.partnerInYear and answer.claimSpouseDonations and line.HH.partner == 1, spouse.line.OWN.donations, 0)
S9.5.source: Schedule 9 line 5: either spouse can claim both spouses' donations

OWN.donations.label: Donations on this return's receipts and entered here
OWN.donations.source: Official receipts (uploaded, or entered), and box 46 of T4 slips

S9.10.label: Donations claimed (within the limit)
S9.10.source: Schedule 9 lines 6 to 10: up to 75% of net income

S9.19.label: Taxable income in the top bracket

S11.8.label: Tuition fees for 2025
S11.8.source: Schedule 11 lines 1 to 8: eligible fees from T2202 box 26, less the Canada training credit claimed

S11.9.label: Unused federal tuition from your 2024 notice of assessment

S11.11.label: Income the tuition amount can reduce to zero tax
S11.11.source: Schedule 11 line 11: taxable income, or above $57,375, federal tax on taxable income ÷ 14.5%

S11.23.label: Tuition you can transfer
S11.23.source: Schedule 11 lines 21 to 23: this year's tuition up to $5,000, less what you used

S11.24.label: Tuition transferred to your spouse or common-law partner
S11.24.formula: if(line.HH.partner == 1 and household.partnerInYear and line.S11.8 > 0, min(answer.tuitionTransfer, line.S11.23), 0)
S11.24.source: Schedule 11 line 24: the amount you designate on your T2202, up to line 23

RESULT.net.label: Refund, less balance owing
RESULT.net.source: The federal refund or balance, and for a Quebec resident the Quebec one (TP-1 lines 478 and 479)

SUGGEST.rrspDeduction.label: RRSP contributions you can deduct for 2025
SUGGEST.rrspDeduction.formula: if(sum(NOA.box1) > 0, min(sum(RRSP.box1) + sum(RRSP.box2) + sum(NOA.box2), sum(NOA.box1)), sum(RRSP.box1) + sum(RRSP.box2) + sum(NOA.box2))
SUGGEST.rrspDeduction.source: RRSP receipts, and the unused contributions and deduction limit on your 2024 notice of assessment

SUGGEST.fhsaDeduction.label: FHSA contributions you can deduct for 2025
SUGGEST.fhsaDeduction.source: Box 18 of your T4FHSA slips: contributions in 2025. Transfers from an RRSP aren't deductible; contributions you didn't deduct in earlier years can be added

MB428.9.label: Manitoba basic personal amount
MB428.9.formula: round((max(0, param.mbBasicPersonalAmount - round(param.mbBasicPersonalAmount * max(0, line.T1.23600 - param.mbBasicPersonalAmountThreshold) / param.mbBasicPersonalAmountRange, 2))) * line.RES.factor, 2)
MB428.9.source: Worksheet MB428, line 58040: $15,780, less the same share of it as net income over $200,000 is of $200,000

MB428.10.label: Manitoba age amount
MB428.10.formula: round((if(person.age >= 65, max(0, param.mbAgeAmountMax - round(max(0, line.T1.23600 - param.mbAgeAmountThreshold) * param.mbAgeAmountRate, 2)), 0)) * line.RES.factor, 2)
MB428.10.source: Worksheet MB428, line 58080: for people born in 1960 or earlier

MB428.13.label: Manitoba spouse or common-law partner amount

MB428.16.label: Manitoba amount for an eligible dependant
MB428.16.source: MB428 lines 14 to 16. The app assumes the child had no income

MB428.17.label: Manitoba amount for infirm dependants age 18 or older
MB428.17.formula: round((if(answer.hasInfirmDependant, if(answer.infirmDependants > 1, unsupported("The Manitoba amount for more than one infirm dependant isn't handled by this app yet"), if(answer.infirmDependants == 0, 0, min(param.mbInfirmMax, max(0, param.mbInfirmBase - answer.infirmDependantIncome)))), 0)) * line.RES.factor, 2)
MB428.17.source: Worksheet MB428, line 58200: $8,720 less the dependant's net income, up to $3,605. The app claims this line, not the caregiver amount (58400), which needs the dependant to have lived with you

MB428.23.label: Volunteer firefighters' amount
MB428.23.source: Manitoba information guide, line 58315: $6,000 when you claim line 31220 of your return

MB428.24.label: Search and rescue volunteers' amount
MB428.24.source: Manitoba information guide, line 58316: $6,000 when you claim line 31240 of your return

MB.fitnessPeople.label: People the Manitoba fitness amount can be claimed for
MB.fitnessPeople.formula: if(person.age < param.mbFitnessAgeLimit, 1, 0) + household.childrenUnder18 + if(line.HH.partner == 1 and household.partnerInYear, if(spouse.person.age >= 18 and spouse.person.age < param.mbFitnessAgeLimit, 1, 0), 0)

MB428.25.label: Fitness amount
MB428.25.formula: if(line.MB.fitnessPeople == 0, 0, if(line.HH.partner == 1 and household.partnerInYear and spouse.person.province == "MB" and answer.physicalActivityFees + spouse.answer.physicalActivityFees > param.mbFitnessMax * line.MB.fitnessPeople, unsupported("Only one of you can claim the Manitoba fitness amount for a person, up to $500 each. Together you claim more: enter each person's fees on one return"), min(answer.physicalActivityFees, param.mbFitnessMax * line.MB.fitnessPeople)))
MB428.25.source: Manitoba information guide, line 58325: fees for a program of physical activity, up to $500 a person. The extra $500 for a person with a disability isn't handled

MB428.26.label: Children's arts amount
MB428.26.formula: if(household.childrenUnder17 == 0, 0, if(line.HH.partner == 1 and household.partnerInYear and spouse.person.province == "MB" and answer.childArtsFees + spouse.answer.childArtsFees > param.mbArtsMax * household.childrenUnder17, unsupported("Only one of you can claim the Manitoba children's arts amount for a child, up to $500 each. Together you claim more: enter each child's fees on one return"), min(answer.childArtsFees, param.mbArtsMax * household.childrenUnder17)))
MB428.26.source: Manitoba information guide, line 58326: up to $500 for each child under 16 at the start of the year (born in 2009 or later). The extra $500 for a child with a disability isn't handled

MB428.27.label: Adoption expenses
MB428.27.formula: if(answer.hasAdoption, if(answer.adoptedChildren > 1 and answer.adoptionExpenses > param.mbAdoptionMax, unsupported("Manitoba adoption expenses over $10,000 for more than one child are claimed child by child, which this app doesn't handle yet"), min(answer.adoptionExpenses, param.mbAdoptionMax)), 0)
MB428.27.source: Manitoba information guide, line 58330: the expenses of line 31300, up to $10,000 for each child

MB428.28.label: CPP, EI, volunteer, fitness, arts and adoption amounts
MB428.28.formula: line.T1.30800 + line.T1.31000 + line.T1.31200 + line.MB428.23 + line.MB428.24 + line.MB428.25 + line.MB428.26 + line.MB428.27
MB428.28.source: MB428 lines 19 to 28: lines 30800, 31000 and 31200 of your return, and lines 23 to 27

MB428.31.label: Manitoba pension income amount
MB428.31.source: MB428 line 31 (58360): eligible pension income, up to $1,000

MB428.34.label: Manitoba disability amount for self
MB428.34.source: MB428 line 34 (58440): $6,180 at 18 or older. The worksheet for someone under 18 isn't handled

MB428.35.label: Manitoba disability amount transferred from a dependant
MB428.35.formula: round((if(answer.hasDisabledDependant, if(answer.disabledChildren > 1 and answer.disabledChildCare > 0, unsupported("Child care for more than one child with a disability is worked out child by child, which this app doesn't handle yet"), answer.disabledChildren * (param.mbDisabilityAmount + param.mbDisabilitySupplementMax) - min(answer.disabledChildren * param.mbDisabilitySupplementMax, max(0, answer.disabledChildCare - param.mbDisabilityCareThreshold)) + answer.disabledAdults * param.mbDisabilityAmount), 0)) * line.RES.factor, 2)
MB428.35.source: Worksheet MB428, line 58480: $6,180, plus up to $3,605 for a child under 18 less care over $2,112. The app assumes the dependant had no income, so all of it transfers (lines 8 to 12)

MB428.36.label: Manitoba credit amounts before tuition and transfers
MB428.36.formula: line.MB428.9 + line.MB428.10 + line.MB428.13 + line.MB428.16 + line.MB428.17 + line.MB428.28 + line.MB428.31 + line.MB428.34 + line.MB428.35
MB428.36.source: MB428 lines 18, 29, 33 and 36. The caregiver amount (line 32) isn't handled

MB428.37.label: Interest paid on your student loans
MB428.37.source: MB428 line 37: line 31900 of your return

MB428.39.label: Tuition and education amounts transferred from a child or grandchild
MB428.39.source: MB428 line 39 (58600): the app uses the amount the student designated to you federally (line 32400)

MB428.40.label: Manitoba amounts transferred from your spouse or common-law partner
MB428.40.source: Schedule MB(S2): their unused Manitoba age, pension, and tuition and education amounts

MB428.48.label: Allowable medical expenses
MB428.48.source: MB428 lines 43 to 48: expenses over whichever is less, $1,728 or 3% of net income

MB428.49.label: Allowable amount of medical expenses for other dependants
MB428.49.formula: if(answer.hasOtherDependantMedical, max(0, answer.otherDependantMedical - min(param.mbMedicalThresholdMax, round(answer.otherDependantIncome * param.medicalThresholdRate, 2))), 0)
MB428.49.source: Worksheet MB428, line 58729: their expenses less line 47 of their MB428 (whichever is less, $1,728 or 3% of their net income)

MB428.51.label: Manitoba credit amounts
MB428.51.formula: line.MB428.36 + line.MB428.37 + line.MB428.38 + line.MB428.39 + line.MB428.40 + line.MB428.41 + line.MB428.48 + line.MB428.49

MB428.53.label: Manitoba credit amounts at the credit rate

MB428.56.label: Manitoba donations credit
MB428.56.source: MB428 lines 54 to 56: Schedule 9 lines 13 and 14 at 10.8% and 17.4%

MB428.72.label: Manitoba tax before the foreign tax credit
MB428.72.source: MB428 lines 67 to 72: minimum tax and labour-sponsored funds aren't handled by this app

MB428.73.label: Provincial foreign tax credit
MB428.73.formula: if(line.FTC.left > 0 and line.T1.23600 > 0, min(line.FTC.left, round(min(line.FTC.netForeign, line.T1.23600) * line.MB428.72 / line.T1.23600, 2), line.MB428.72), 0)
MB428.73.source: Form T2036, line 5, with note 4: Manitoba tax before the provincial foreign tax credit (MB428 line 72)

MB428.82.label: Manitoba tax
MB428.82.source: MB428 lines 74 to 82: the Manitoba investment tax credits aren't handled by this app

MB.higherIncome.label: This return claims the Manitoba credits for the children (1 for yes)
MB.higherIncome.formula: if(line.HH.partner == 0, 1, if(not household.partnerInYear, if(line.T1.23600 >= line.HH.spouseNetIncome, 1, 0), if(spouse.person.province != "MB", 1, if(line.T1.23600 > line.HH.spouseNetIncome, 1, if(line.T1.23600 < line.HH.spouseNetIncome, 0, if(person.age > spouse.person.age, 1, if(person.age < spouse.person.age, 0, if(person.role == "self", 1, 0))))))))
MB.higherIncome.source: Manitoba information guide, Schedule MB428-A line 9: only the spouse or partner with the higher net income can claim it

MB.claimsPersonalCredit.label: This return claims the Manitoba personal tax credit for the family (1 for yes)
MB.claimsPersonalCredit.formula: if(line.HH.partner == 0, 1, if(not household.partnerInYear, 1, if(spouse.person.province != "MB", 1, if(spouse.line.MB428.40 > 0 and line.MB428.10 > 0 and not (line.MB428.40 > 0 and spouse.line.MB428.10 > 0), 0, if(line.MB428.40 > 0 and spouse.line.MB428.10 > 0 and not (spouse.line.MB428.40 > 0 and line.MB428.10 > 0), 1, line.MB.higherIncome)))))
MB.claimsPersonalCredit.source: Manitoba information guide, Form MB479, personal tax credit: only one of a couple claims it, for both

MB.disabledDependants.label: Dependants whose disability amount you or your spouse claim (line 58480)
MB.disabledDependants.formula: if(answer.hasDisabledDependant, answer.disabledChildren + answer.disabledAdults, 0) + if(line.HH.partner == 1 and household.partnerInYear, if(spouse.answer.hasDisabledDependant, spouse.answer.disabledChildren + spouse.answer.disabledAdults, 0), 0)

MB.infirmDependants.label: Infirm dependants 18 or older you or your spouse claim (line 58200)
MB.infirmDependants.formula: if(answer.hasInfirmDependant, answer.infirmDependants, 0) + if(line.HH.partner == 1 and household.partnerInYear, if(spouse.answer.hasInfirmDependant, spouse.answer.infirmDependants, 0), 0)

MB428A.9.label: Amount for dependent children
MB428A.9.source: MB428-A line 9: children born in 2007 or later, other than the one claimed as an eligible dependant

MB428A.6.label: Disability amount for spouse or common-law partner
MB428A.6.formula: if(line.MB428.40 > 0 and spouse.line.MB428.34 > 0 and line.MBS2.12 > spouse.line.MBS11.20, param.mbFamilyBenefitDisability, 0)
MB428A.6.source: MB428-A line 6: when you transfer their disability amount on MB(S2) line 3 and line 12 is more than line 4

MB428A.7.label: Disability amount for self or for a dependant
MB428A.7.source: MB428-A line 7: yours, and each dependant's on line 58480, claimed by the spouse with the higher net income

MB428A.8.label: Amount for disabled dependants born in 2007 or earlier
