PE428.66.source: PE428 line 66: line 101 of their PE428

PE428.67.label: Prince Edward Island tax after your spouse's unused reduction

PE428.73.label: Adjusted family income
PE428.73.source: PE428 lines 68 to 73: both net incomes. UCCB amounts aren't handled

PE428.78.label: Age reduction for your spouse or common-law partner
PE428.78.source: PE428 line 78: $250 if they were born in 1960 or earlier. Their age is known only when their return is prepared here

PE428.81.label: Prince Edward Island tax reductions
PE428.81.formula: param.peTaxReductionBasic + if(person.age >= 65, param.peTaxReductionAge, 0) + if(line.HH.partner == 1, param.peTaxReductionBasic, 0) + line.PE428.78 + if(line.PE428.16 > 0, param.peTaxReductionBasic, 0) + param.peTaxReductionChild * max(0, household.childrenUnder19 - if(line.PE428.16 > 0, 1, 0))

PE428.86.label: Prince Edward Island tax reduction clawback
PE428.86.source: PE428 lines 82 to 86: 5% of adjusted family income over $22,650

PE428.87.label: Prince Edward Island low-income tax reduction

PE428.88.label: Prince Edward Island tax after the low-income tax reduction

PE428.89.label: Provincial foreign tax credit
PE428.89.formula: if(line.FTC.left > 0 and line.T1.23600 > 0, min(line.FTC.left, round(min(line.FTC.netForeign, line.T1.23600) * line.PE428.88 / line.T1.23600, 2), line.PE428.88), 0)
PE428.89.source: Form T2036, line 5, with note 4: Prince Edward Island tax before the foreign tax credit

PE428.90.label: Prince Edward Island tax after the foreign tax credit

PE428.92.label: Prince Edward Island political contribution tax credit
PE428.92.source: Worksheet PE428, line 92: 75% of the first $100, 50% of the next $450, 33.33% of the next $600; $500 over $1,150

PE428.97.label: Prince Edward Island tax
PE428.97.source: PE428 lines 93 to 97. The equity tax credit isn't handled

PE428.98.label: Volunteer firefighter and volunteer search and rescue personnel tax credit
PE428.98.source: PE428 line 98 (63510): $1,000 when you meet the rules for line 31220 or 31240 of your return

PE428.101.label: Unused low-income tax reduction your spouse or common-law partner can claim
PE428.101.source: PE428 lines 99 to 101: line 87 less line 65

PES11.1.label: Unused Prince Edward Island tuition and education amounts from your 2024 notice of assessment

PES11.5.label: 2025 Prince Edward Island tuition and education amounts
PES11.5.formula: line.S11.8 + min(12, sum(T2202.box24)) * param.peEducationPartTime + min(12, sum(T2202.box25)) * param.peEducationFullTime
PES11.5.source: PE(S11) lines 2 to 5: the tuition on federal Schedule 11 line 8, and $120 a month part-time or $400 full-time (T2202 boxes 24 and 25)

PES11.9.label: Income the tuition amount can reduce to zero Prince Edward Island tax
PES11.9.formula: max(0, if(line.T1.26000 <= param.peFirstBracketTop, line.T1.26000, round(line.PE428.8 / param.peCreditRate, 2)) - line.PE428.34)
PES11.9.source: PE(S11) lines 7 to 9: taxable income, or above $33,328 Prince Edward Island tax on it ÷ 9.5%, less PE428 line 34

PES11.13.label: Prince Edward Island tuition and education amounts claimed for 2025

PES11.19.label: Prince Edward Island tuition and education amounts you can transfer
PES11.19.source: PE(S11) lines 17 to 19: this year's amounts up to $5,000, less what you used

PES11.20.label: Prince Edward Island tuition and education amounts transferred to your spouse or common-law partner
PES11.20.formula: if(line.HH.partner == 1 and household.partnerInYear and line.PES11.5 > 0, min(answer.tuitionTransfer, line.PES11.19), 0)
PES11.20.source: PE(S11) line 20: the amount you designate on your T2202 (the same as federally), up to line 19

PES2.5.label: Their Prince Edward Island age, pension and disability amounts, and the tuition they designate to you

PES2.6.label: Their taxable income, for the transfer

PES2.11.label: Their adjusted taxable income
PES2.11.source: PE(S2) lines 7 to 11: their lines 58040, 24 and 58560

PES2.12.label: Prince Edward Island amounts transferred from your spouse

QCB.20.label: Amount for a person living alone
QCB.20.source: Schedule B, line 20: living all year in a dwelling alone, or only with people under 18 or student children

QCB.22.label: Age amount
QCB.22.source: Schedule B, line 22: born before January 1, 1961

QCB.23.label: Age amount of your spouse
QCB.23.source: Schedule B, line 23: your spouse born before January 1, 1961

QCB.27.label: Amount for retirement income
QCB.27.formula: min(param.qcRetirementMax, round(max(0, line.TP1.122 + line.TP1.123 - line.TP1.245) * param.qcRetirementFactor, 2))
QCB.27.source: Schedule B, work chart, lines 1 to 9: lines 122 and 123 less line 245, × 1.25, maximum $3,470

QCB.28.label: Amount for your spouse's retirement income
QCB.28.source: Schedule B, line 28: the work chart for your spouse

QCB.30.label: Schedule B amounts
QCB.30.source: Schedule B, line 30: lines 20 through 28 (line 21 isn't handled)

QCB.32.label: Amount to which you or your spouse is entitled

QC.ownMedical.label: Medical expenses on this return's receipts and Quebec slips
QC.ownMedical.source: Guide, line 381: receipts, and the private health plan premiums of box J and box 235 of the RL-1 and box 235 of the RL-2

QC.claimsMedical.label: This return claims the couple's medical expenses (1 for yes)
QC.claimsMedical.formula: if(line.QC.couple == 1, if(line.QC.work > spouse.line.QC.work or (line.QC.work == spouse.line.QC.work and person.role == "self"), 1, 0), 1)
QC.claimsMedical.source: Guide, line 381: either spouse may claim the couple's expenses, less 3% of family income either way; the one with the higher work income can also get the refundable credit

QCB.44.label: Refundable medical credit before reduction
QCB.44.source: Schedule B, lines 41 to 44: line 40 and the disability supports deduction (as on federal line 21500), × 25%, maximum $1,466

QCB.48.label: Reduction of the refundable medical credit
QCB.48.source: Schedule B, lines 45 to 48: 5% of family income over $28,335

QCB.50.label: Refundable tax credit for medical expenses
QCB.50.formula: if(person.residentAllYear and person.age >= 18 and line.QC.work >= param.qcMedicalRefundMinWork, max(0, line.QCB.44 - line.QCB.48), 0)
QCB.50.source: Schedule B, Part D, line 50: resident all year, 18 or older, with work income of $3,750 or more

QCC.own.label: Childcare expenses this return paid
QCC.own.formula: if(household.childrenUnder17 > 0, max(0, sum(RL24.boxE) + answer.qcChildCareReceipts - sum(RL1.box201) - sum(RL5.boxJ)), 0)
QCC.own.source: Schedule C, lines 26.1 to 41: box E of the RL-24 slips and the receipts without one, less the allowance in box 201 of the RL-1 or box J of the RL-5

QCC.41.label: Childcare expenses qualifying for the tax credit
QCC.41.source: Schedule C, line 41: the couple's expenses

QCC.50.label: Childcare expense limit
QCC.50.source: Schedule C, lines 44 to 50: $12,275 for each child born after 2018 and $6,180 for each child born after 2008 (the $16,800 limit for a child with an impairment isn't handled)

QCC.85.label: Childcare expenses counted
QCC.85.source: Schedule C, line 85: line 41 or line 50, whichever is less

QCC.92.label: Childcare credit rate
QCC.92.source: Schedule C, line 92: the rate for the family income

QCC.94.label: Couple's tax credit for childcare expenses

QCC.claims.label: This return claims the couple's childcare credit (1 for yes)
QCC.claims.formula: if(line.QC.couple == 1, if(line.QCC.own > spouse.line.QCC.own or (line.QCC.own == spouse.line.QCC.own and person.role == "self"), 1, 0), 1)

QCD.12.label: Lived alone in a dwelling throughout 2025 (1 for yes)

QCD.33.label: Tenants who signed the lease (RL-31 box B)
QCD.33.source: Schedule D, line 33: box B of the RL-31 slip issued in your name

QCD.check.label: Schedule D answers that don't fit together
QCD.check.formula: if(count(RL31.boxB) > 0 and answer.qcHomeOwner, unsupported("Schedule D takes a tenant's RL-31 or an owner's roll number, not both: remove the RL-31 or say you didn't own your home"), if(answer.qcHomeOwner and answer.qcHomeOwners < 1, unsupported("Enter how many owners live in the home you own (Schedule D, line 36)"), 0))
QCD.check.source: Schedule D, Part A: lines 32 and 33 for a tenant, lines 35 and 36 for an owner

QCF.18.label: Total income other than employment income

QCF.34.label: Income not subject to the contribution
QCF.34.formula: line.TP1.114 + max(0, line.TP1.128 - line.TP1.166 - line.TP1.167) + line.TP1.142 + line.TP1.147
QCF.34.source: Schedule F, lines 20 to 34: the OAS pension, the dividend gross-up, taxable support and social assistance

QCF.68.label: Deductions
QCF.68.formula: line.QCR.26 + line.QCU.101 + line.QCU.103 + if(line.QCU.33 > 0, min(line.QCU.94 - line.QCU.48, line.QCU.99), 0) + line.TP1.245 + line.TP1.225 + line.TP1.231
QCF.68.source: Schedule F, lines 41 to 68: Schedule R line 26, Schedule U lines 101, 103 and 115, and lines 245, 225 and 231

QCJ.34.label: Home-support services included in your rent
QCJ.34.formula: if(person.age >= param.seniorCreditAge, if(answer.hasHomeSupport, if(answer.homeSupportRent > 0, round(clamp(answer.homeSupportRent, param.homeSupportRentMin, param.homeSupportRentMax) * param.homeSupportRentShare, 2) * answer.homeSupportRentMonths, 0), 0), 0)
QCJ.34.source: Schedule J, Part A, section 2, lines 30 to 34: 5% of the monthly rent (at least $600, at most $1,200) times the months

QCJ.74.label: Home-support services you paid
QCJ.74.source: Schedule J, Part B, lines 50 to 74

QCJ.75.label: Cost of home-support services
QCJ.75.formula: min(if(line.QC.couple == 1, if(spouse.person.age >= param.seniorCreditAge, param.homeSupportMaxCouple, param.homeSupportMaxSingle), param.homeSupportMaxSingle), line.QCJ.34 + line.QCJ.74)
QCJ.75.source: Schedule J, line 75, and guide, line 458: at most $19,500, or $39,000 for a couple of seniors

QCJ.89.label: Reduction based on family income
QCJ.89.formula: round(max(0, min(line.QC.family, param.homeSupportSecondThreshold) - param.homeSupportThreshold) * param.homeSupportReductionRate, 2) + round(max(0, line.QC.family - param.homeSupportSecondThreshold) * param.homeSupportSecondReductionRate, 2)
QCJ.89.source: Work Chart 458, lines 10 to 16: 3% of family income from $71,010 to $115,035, and 7% above

QCJ.90.label: Tax credit for home-support services for seniors
QCJ.90.formula: if(line.QC.couple == 1 and person.age >= param.seniorCreditAge and answer.hasHomeSupport and spouse.person.age >= param.seniorCreditAge and spouse.answer.hasHomeSupport, unsupported("Only one spouse claims the home-support credit for the couple: enter the services on one return"), max(0, line.QCJ.88 - line.QCJ.89))

QCK.40.label: Family income for the drug premium

QCK.46.label: Income not subject to the premium
QCK.46.formula: if(line.HH.partner == 1, param.drugIncomeCouple + if(household.childrenUnder18 >= 2, param.drugChildrenCouple, if(household.childrenUnder18 == 1, param.drugChildCouple, 0)), param.drugIncomeSingle + if(household.childrenUnder18 >= 2, param.drugChildrenSingle, if(household.childrenUnder18 == 1, param.drugChildSingle, 0)))
QCK.46.source: Schedule K, lines 41 to 46 (a dependent child: under 18 at the end of the year)

QCK.48.label: Income used to calculate the premium

QCK.84.label: Premium for a full year
QCK.84.formula: if(line.QCK.48 > param.drugTableTop, param.drugPremiumMax, if(line.HH.partner == 1, if(line.QCK.48 <= param.drugTableBreak, round(line.QCK.48 * param.drugRateCoupleLow, 2), min(param.drugPremiumMax, param.drugBaseCouple + round((line.QCK.48 - param.drugTableBreak) * param.drugRateCoupleHigh, 2))), if(line.QCK.48 <= param.drugTableBreak, round(line.QCK.48 * param.drugRateSingleLow, 2), min(param.drugPremiumMax, param.drugBaseSingle + round((line.QCK.48 - param.drugTableBreak) * param.drugRateSingleHigh, 2)))))
QCK.84.source: Schedule K, Part C, lines 77 to 84

QCK.60.label: Months from January to June covered by a group plan

QCK.61.label: Months from July to December covered by a group plan

QCK.62.label: Months with no premium to pay
QCK.62.formula: if(line.QCK.60 > 6 or line.QCK.61 > 6, unsupported("Each half of the year has 6 months: check the months your group drug plan covered you"), line.QCK.60 + line.QCK.61)

QCK.86.label: Premium for the months without a group plan

QCK.89.label: Most premium for those months
QCK.89.source: Schedule K, lines 87 to 89: $755 less $62.00 a month from January to June and $63.83 a month from July to December

QCK.90.label: Drug insurance premium
QCK.90.source: Schedule K, line 90: line 86 or line 89, whichever is less

QCP.49.label: Your spouse's work income
QCP.49.formula: if(line.HH.partner == 1, if(household.partnerInYear, if(spouse.person.province == "QC", spouse.line.QC.work, spouse.line.CWB.working), if(line.QC.family < param.workPremiumMaxFamilyCouple, unsupported("The work premium for a couple needs your spouse's work income: prepare their return here too"), 0)), 0)
QCP.49.source: Schedule P, line 49; a couple whose family income is over the most can't get the premium, so the spouse's income isn't needed

QCP.72.label: Work income counted
QCP.72.formula: max(0, min(line.QCP.64, if(line.HH.partner == 1, param.workPremiumCapCouple, param.workPremiumCapSingle)) - if(line.HH.partner == 1, param.workPremiumExclusionCouple, param.workPremiumExclusionSingle))
QCP.72.source: Schedule P, Part E, lines 66 to 72

QCP.76.label: Work premium before reduction
QCP.76.formula: round(line.QCP.72 * if(household.childrenUnder18 > 0, if(line.HH.partner == 1, param.workPremiumRateChildCouple, param.workPremiumRateChildSingle), param.workPremiumRate), 2)
QCP.76.source: Schedule P, lines 74 and 76: 25% (couple) or 30% (single parent) with a designated dependent child (a child under 18 who lived with you), else 11.6%

QCP.83.label: Reduction based on family income
QCP.83.formula: round(max(0, line.QC.family - if(line.HH.partner == 1, param.workPremiumCapCouple, param.workPremiumCapSingle)) * param.workPremiumReductionRate, 2)

QCP.90.label: Tax credits respecting the work premium
QCP.90.formula: if(line.QC.couple == 1, if(line.QC.work > spouse.line.QC.work or (line.QC.work == spouse.line.QC.work and person.role == "self"), line.QCP.84, 0), line.QCP.84)
QCP.90.source: Schedule P, lines 85 to 90: a couple's premium, claimed by the spouse with the higher work income (line 86 is the other's line 89)

QCQ.20.label: Eligible retirement income
QCQ.20.source: Schedule Q, lines 10 to 20: line 122 (no amount transferred to a plan or deducted)

QCQ.58.label: Quebec income tax withholding transferred to your spouse
QCQ.58.source: Schedule Q, lines 50 to 58: the tax withheld on the RL-2 (box J) × line 22 ÷ line 20

QCR.14.label: Employment income subject to QPIP
QCR.14.formula: if(count(RL1.boxI) == 0, sum(RL1.boxA), if(count(RL1.boxI) >= count(RL1.boxA), sum(RL1.boxI), unsupported("Some of your RL-1 slips show box I and some don't. Enter box I on each slip: the amount from box A when box I is blank")))
QCR.14.source: Schedule R, line 14: box I of the RL-1 slips (box A if blank)

QCR.24.label: QPIP premium on self-employment
QCR.24.formula: if(line.QCR.12 + line.QCR.14 < param.qpipMinimum, 0, min(param.qpipMaxSelfEmployed, round(min(line.QCR.12, line.QCR.20) * param.qpipSelfEmployedRate, 2)))
QCR.24.source: Schedule R, lines 22 and 24: 0.878%, maximum $860.44; none when business and employment income are less than $2,000

QCT.41.label: Tuition fees for 2025
QCT.41.source: Schedule T, lines 40.6 to 41: box B of the RL-8 slips, if more than $100, less the Canada training credit (federal line 45350)

QCT.44_1.label: Tuition fees for the 8% credit
QCT.44_1.source: Schedule T, lines 43 to 44.1: with the unused fees of earlier years

QCT.45.label: Tax credit for tuition or examination fees available

QCU.11.label: First additional part of the QPP contribution

QCU.14_4.label: Pensionable salary over the exemption
QCU.14_4.formula: min(max(0, min(line.TP1.98_1, param.qppMaxPensionable) - param.qppExemption), param.qppMaxPensionable - param.qppExemption)

QCU.17_5.label: QPP contributions over those required, and the additional contribution

QCU.21.label: Second additional contributions required
QCU.21.formula: round(min(max(0, line.TP1.98_1 - param.qppMaxPensionable), param.qppAdditionalMaxPensionable - param.qppMaxPensionable) * param.qppSecondRate, 2)
QCU.21.source: Schedule U, lines 18.5 to 21: 4% of pensionable salary between $71,300 and $81,200

QCU.23.label: Deduction for QPP contributions on employment income

QCU.33.label: Net business income for QPP
QCU.33.source: Schedule U, lines 30 to 33: line 27 of Schedule L, 0 if negative. QPP is paid from 18 until the year you turn 73 (Schedule U, instructions)

QCU.40.label: Earnings your employee contributions cover, with the exemption
QCU.40.source: Schedule U, lines 34 to 40: lines 98 and 98.2 ÷ 6.4%, plus $3,500

QCU.48.label: QPP base and first additional contribution on self-employment
QCU.48.source: Schedule U, lines 44 to 48: 12.8%, up to the maximum pensionable earnings the employee contributions leave

QCU.71.label: Base and first additional contributions required on all earnings
QCU.71.formula: min(param.qppMaxEmployee, round(max(0, min(param.qppMaxPensionable, line.QCU.33 + line.TP1.98_1) - param.qppExemption) * param.qppEmployeeRate, 2))

QCU.94.label: QPP contribution on self-employment, before the limit
QCU.94.formula: line.QCU.48 + round(min(max(0, line.QCU.33 + min(line.TP1.98_1, line.QCU.40) - param.qppMaxPensionable), param.qppAdditionalMaxPensionable - param.qppMaxPensionable, line.QCU.33) * param.qppSecondSelfEmployedRate, 2)
QCU.94.source: Schedule U, lines 75 to 94: line 48 plus 8% of the self-employment earnings between $71,300 and $81,200 (line 92)

QCU.95.label: Contributions required on all earnings, employee share
QCU.95.formula: line.QCU.71 + round(max(0, min(param.qppAdditionalMaxPensionable, line.TP1.98_1 + line.QCU.33) - param.qppMaxPensionable) * param.qppSecondRate, 2)

QCU.99.label: QPP contribution on income from self-employment
QCU.99.formula: if(line.QCU.33 > 0 and line.TP1.98 > line.QCU.71, unsupported("QPP contributions deducted by employers over the maximum, with self-employment income (Schedule U, lines 72 to 74), aren't handled by this app yet"), min(line.QCU.94, line.QCU.98))
QCU.99.source: Schedule U, line 99: line 94 or line 98, whichever is less

QCU.101.label: Deduction for half the base contribution on self-employment

QCU.103.label: Deduction for the first additional contribution on self-employment

QCU.111.label: All pensionable earnings over the exemption
QCU.111.formula: min(param.qppMaxPensionable - param.qppExemption, max(0, line.QCU.33 + line.TP1.98_1 - param.qppExemption))

QCU.124.label: QPP deduction
QCU.124.formula: line.QCU.101 + line.QCU.103 + min(round(line.TP1.98 * param.qppFirstShare, 2), round(line.QCU.111 * param.qppFirstRate, 2)) + min(line.QCU.94 - line.QCU.48, line.QCU.99) + min(max(0, line.TP1.98 - round(line.QCU.111 * param.qppEmployeeRate, 2)) + line.TP1.98_2, round(min(max(0, line.TP1.98_1 + line.QCU.33 - param.qppMaxPensionable), param.qppAdditionalMaxPensionable - param.qppMaxPensionable) * param.qppSecondRate, 2))
QCU.124.source: Schedule U, lines 100 to 124: lines 114 (101, 103 and 113), 115 and 123

QC.childActivities.label: Tax credit for children's activities
QC.childActivities.formula: if(household.childrenUnder17 - household.childrenUnder6 > 0 and line.QC.family <= param.childActivitiesMaxIncome, round(min(answer.childActivityFees, param.childActivitiesMaxFees * (household.childrenUnder17 - household.childrenUnder6)) * param.childActivitiesRate, 2), 0)
QC.childActivities.source: Guide, line 462, point 25: 20% of fees up to $500 for each child born from 2009 to 2019, with family income of $168,470 or less (the extra for a child with an impairment isn't handled)

QC.seniorAssistance.label: Senior assistance tax credit
QC.seniorAssistance.formula: if(line.QC.couple == 1 and person.role == "spouse", 0, max(0, param.seniorAssistanceMax * (if(person.age >= param.seniorCreditAge, 1, 0) + if(line.QC.couple == 1, if(spouse.person.age >= param.seniorCreditAge, 1, 0), 0)) - if(person.age >= param.seniorCreditAge or (line.QC.couple == 1 and spouse.person.age >= param.seniorCreditAge), round(max(0, line.QC.family - if(line.HH.partner == 1, param.seniorAssistanceThresholdCouple, param.seniorAssistanceThresholdSingle)) * param.seniorAssistanceRate, 2), 0)))
QC.seniorAssistance.source: Guide, line 463: $2,000 for each eligible person 70 or older, less 5.40% of family income over $45,270 (with a spouse) or $27,835. A couple's credit is claimed on the return of the person preparing

QC.couple.label: Both spouses file a Quebec return prepared here (1 for yes)

QC.spouseNet.label: Your spouse's net income, for the Quebec family income
QC.spouseNet.formula: if(line.HH.partner == 1, if(household.partnerInYear, if(spouse.person.province == "QC", spouse.line.TP1.275, spouse.line.T1.23600), answer.spouseNetIncome), 0)
QC.spouseNet.source: TP-1 line 51: your spouse's net income (line 275 of their TP-1); for a spouse who doesn't file one, their federal net income

QC.family.label: Family income
QC.family.source: Schedules B, C, J, K and P, Part A or C: line 275 of your return plus line 275 of your spouse's return

QC.work.label: Work income
QC.work.source: Work Chart 201, lines 1 to 8, and Schedule P, line 29: line 101 less box 211 of the RL-1, plus net business income (no losses)

QC.scope.label: Quebec return cases this app doesn't handle
QC.scope.formula: if(not person.residentAllYear, unsupported("A Quebec return for a year you moved to or from Canada isn't handled by this app yet"), if(count(T4.box14) > count(RL1.boxA), unsupported("A Quebec resident's employer in Quebec issues an RL-1 with each T4: upload it. Employment outside Quebec (a T4 without an RL-1, Schedule R Part B) isn't handled by this app yet"), if(answer.hasRentalIncome, unsupported("Rental income on the Quebec return (form TP-128-V) isn't handled by this app yet"), if(answer.hasForeignIncome, unsupported("Foreign income on the Quebec return (the foreign tax credit, Schedule E) isn't handled by this app yet"), if(sum(T4AOAS.box21) > 0, unsupported("Net federal supplements on the Quebec return (lines 148 and 295) aren't handled by this app yet"), if(answer.hasMovingExpenses, unsupported("Moving expenses on the Quebec return (form TP-348-V) aren't handled by this app yet"), 0))))))

TP1.97.label: QPIP premium
TP1.97.source: TP-1 line 97: box H of your RL-1 slips

TP1.98_1.source: TP-1 line 98.1: box G of your RL-1 slips

TP1.98_2.source: TP-1 line 98.2: box B.B of your RL-1 slips

TP1.101.label: Employment income
TP1.101.source: TP-1 line 101: box A of your RL-1 slips

TP1.110.label: Parental insurance benefits
TP1.110.source: TP-1 line 110: box A of the RL-6 slip

TP1.119.label: QPP or CPP benefits
TP1.119.source: TP-1 line 119: box C of the RL-2 slip for QPP benefits; a CPP pension (Service Canada issues no RL-2) from box 20 of the T4A(P)

TP1.122.label: Payments from a pension plan, an RRSP or a RRIF, or annuities
TP1.122.source: TP-1 line 122: boxes A and B of the RL-2 slip

TP1.123.label: Retirement income transferred by your spouse

TP1.166.label: Actual amount of eligible dividends
TP1.166.source: TP-1 line 166: box A1 of the RL-3 slip and box C1 of the RL-16 slip

TP1.167.label: Actual amount of ordinary dividends
TP1.167.source: TP-1 line 167: box A2 of the RL-3 slip and box C2 of the RL-16 slip

TP1.128.source: TP-1 line 128: box B of the RL-3 slip and box I of the RL-16 slip

TP1.130.formula: sum(RL3.boxD) + sum(RL3.boxE) + sum(RL3.boxF) + sum(RL16.boxE) + sum(RL16.boxF) + sum(RL16.boxG)
TP1.130.source: TP-1 line 130: boxes D, E and F of the RL-3 slip; boxes E, F and G of the RL-16 slip

TP1.393.source: Work Chart 395, line 1: monetary donations made in 2025. Whoever claims both spouses' donations on the federal return claims them here too

TP1.395.source: Work Chart 395, lines 2 to 12: 20% of the first $200; 25.75% of the rest up to taxable income over $129,590; 24% of what remains

TP1.414.source: Work Chart 414: 85% of the first $50 and 75% of the rest, of up to $200 of contributions (the credit is then at most $155)

TP1.432.source: TP-1 line 432: line 430 minus line 431; 0 if negative

TP1.446.formula: if(line.QCF.70 <= param.hsfThreshold, 0, if(line.QCF.70 <= param.hsfSecondThreshold, min(param.hsfFirstMax, round((line.QCF.70 - param.hsfThreshold) * param.hsfRate, 2)), min(param.hsfMax, param.hsfFirstMax + round((line.QCF.70 - param.hsfSecondThreshold) * param.hsfRate, 2))))
TP1.446.source: Schedule F, Part B: 1% of income over $18,130 (at most $150), or $150 plus 1% over $63,060 (at most $1,000)

TP1.449.source: Schedule K, situations 14 (a group plan all year), 32 (no spouse and line 275 of $19,890 or less) and 34 (family income of $32,240 or less); 0 when the premium is payable

TP1.450.formula: line.TP1.432 + line.TP1.439 + line.TP1.441 + line.TP1.445 + line.TP1.446 + line.TP1.447

TP1.452.formula: if(line.QCU.33 > 0, max(0, line.TP1.98 + line.TP1.98_2 - param.qppMaxEmployeeTotal), max(0, line.TP1.98 - round(line.QCU.14_4 * param.qppEmployeeRate, 2)) + max(0, line.TP1.98_2 - line.QCU.21))
TP1.452.source: Guide, line 452: the contributions deducted (lines 98 and 98.2) less those required on the pensionable salary (Schedule U lines 17.2 and 21); with self-employment, the part over $4,735.20

TP1.455.source: Schedule C, line 98: the couple's credit, claimed here on the return of the spouse who paid more of the expenses (line 96 is then the other's 0)

TP1.456.label: Tax credits respecting the work premium

TP1.457.source: Guide, line 457: the premiums deducted (line 97) less 0.494% of the insurable salary up to $98,000; all of line 97 when employment and business income are less than $2,000

SK428.10.source: Worksheet SK428, line 58080: for people born in 1960 or earlier

SK428.16.source: SK428 lines 14 to 16. The app assumes the child had no income

SK428.17.formula: round((if(answer.hasInfirmDependant, if(answer.infirmDependants > 1, unsupported("The Saskatchewan amount for more than one infirm dependant isn't handled by this app yet"), if(answer.infirmDependants == 0, 0, if(answer.infirmDependantHome == "with_you", 0, min(param.skDependantAmountMax, max(0, param.skInfirmDependantBase - answer.infirmDependantIncome))))), 0)) * line.RES.factor, 2)

SK428.19.source: SK428 line 19 (58220): for people born in 1960 or earlier, whatever their income

SK428.34.source: Worksheet SK428, line 58400: for a dependant with an impairment who lived with you, $33,094 less their net income, up to $13,986

YT428.23.source: YT428 line 23 (58330): the rules and the $19,580 maximum of line 31300 (canada.ca/yt-tax-info)

YT428.24.label: CPP, EI, Canada employment, children's arts and adoption amounts

YT428.25.label: Yukon pension income amount

YT428.26.label: Yukon disability amount for self
YT428.26.source: YT428 line 26 (58440): line 31600 of your return

YT428.27.label: Yukon disability amount transferred from a dependant
YT428.27.source: YT428 line 27 (58480): line 31800 of your return

hasEmploymentIncome.help: A T4 from each employer you worked for in 2025.

hasRl1.help: An RL-1 from each employer in Quebec, which also gives you a T4. The Quebec return reads the RL-1.

hasInvestmentIncome.help: A T5 from each bank, credit union or broker that paid you $50 or more.

hasRl3.help: An RL-3 from each bank, credit union or broker, which also gives you a T5.

hasTrustIncome.help: A T3 from each mutual fund or trust held outside an RRSP or TFSA.

hasRl16.ask: Mutual fund or trust income, Quebec slip (RL-16)
hasRl16.help: An RL-16 from each mutual fund or trust, which also gives you a T3.

hasSoldInvestments.ask: Sold shares, bonds or fund units
hasSoldInvestments.help: A T5008 from each broker, for sales outside an RRSP or TFSA.

hasCppBenefits.help: A T4A(P) from Service Canada, for a CPP retirement, survivor or disability pension.

hasPensionIncome.ask: A pension, annuity, scholarship or other T4A income
hasPensionIncome.help: A T4A from each pension plan, school or other payer.

hasRl2.ask: Pension, RRSP, RRIF or QPP payments, Quebec slip (RL-2)
hasRl2.help: An RL-2 from each pension plan, RRSP or RRIF issuer, and from Retraite Québec for QPP benefits. They also give you a T4A, T4RSP, T4RIF or T4A(P).

hasRrifIncome.help: A T4RIF from each registered retirement income fund you were paid from.

hasEiBenefits.help: A T4E from Service Canada, for EI regular, sickness, maternity or parental benefits.

hasRl6.help: An RL-6 from the Québec parental insurance plan, for maternity, paternity, parental or adoption benefits.

hasSelfEmployment.help: Income from your own business, profession, farm or fishing, freelancing or gig work (Form T2125, T2042 or T2121). Attach the form to a paper return.

optionLabels.business: Business (a shop, trade or gig work)

selfEmploymentGross.help: What you were paid in 2025, without GST/HST you collected.

selfEmploymentExpenses.help: Supplies, rent, phone, travel, fees and other costs of earning it. Not capital cost allowance, which is asked next.

businessCcaClass.help: Depreciation of property you use in the business: equipment, a vehicle, computers or a building. This app works out one class.

optionLabels.class10: Class 10 (30%), a vehicle, other than class 10.1
optionLabels.class10_1: Class 10.1 (30%), a car that cost more than $38,000

businessUccStart.ask: Undepreciated capital cost at the start of 2025
businessUccStart.help: The class's balance at the end of 2024, from last year's form (Area A, last column). 0 for property first bought in 2025.

businessCcaAdditions.ask: Property bought and put in use in 2025
businessCcaAdditions.help: Its cost. For a class 10.1 car, at most $38,000 plus GST/HST and PST.

businessCcaDispositions.ask: Property of the class sold in 2025
businessCcaDispositions.help: What you got for it, up to what it cost you. If you sold everything in the class, the terminal loss isn't worked out here.

businessCcaPersonalUse.help: For a car you also drive for yourself, the share of the kilometres that were personal. That part of the allowance isn't deducted. Leave it empty for none.

businessCcaLimit.ask: Most capital cost allowance to claim, if less than the maximum
businessCcaLimit.help: Leave it empty to claim the most allowed. What you don't claim stays in the class for later years.

hasRentalIncome.help: Rent from a property you own (Form T776). If you own it with someone, enter your share.

rentalExpenses.help: Mortgage interest, property tax, insurance, repairs, utilities you paid, and fees. Not capital cost allowance, which is asked next.

rentalCcaClass.help: Depreciation of the rental building, or of its furniture and appliances. It can't make or increase a rental loss. This app works out one class.

rentalUccStart.ask: Undepreciated capital cost at the start of 2025
rentalUccStart.help: The class's balance at the end of 2024, from last year's Form T776 (Area A, last column). 0 for property first bought in 2025.

rentalCcaAdditions.ask: Property bought and put in use in 2025
rentalCcaAdditions.help: Its cost, the rental part only. Not the land, which isn't depreciated.

rentalCcaDispositions.ask: Property of the class sold in 2025
rentalCcaDispositions.help: What you got for the building (not the land), up to what it cost you. If you sold everything in the class, the terminal loss isn't worked out here.

rentalCcaLimit.ask: Most capital cost allowance to claim, if less than the maximum
rentalCcaLimit.help: Leave it empty to claim the most allowed. What you don't claim stays in the class for later years.

hasForeignIncome.help: Interest, dividends or employment income earned abroad, in Canadian dollars. Foreign tax paid on it gives a foreign tax credit (Form T2209).

hasForeignProperty.ask: Property outside Canada that cost more than $100,000
hasForeignProperty.help: Foreign bank accounts, shares or real estate (not a home you use) that cost more than $100,000 in total at any time in 2025.
hasForeignProperty.note: File Form T1135, Foreign Income Verification Statement, with your return. It reports the property; it doesn't change your tax. This app doesn't prepare it.

soldProperty.ask: Sold your home or other real estate
soldProperty.help: The sale of a home, cottage or rental property in 2025 (Schedule 3; Form T2091(IND) for a home).

propertyUse.help: For your home, file Form T2091(IND) and tick the box at line 17900 of Schedule 3: box 1 for every year, box 2 for some years.

optionLabels.principal_residence: Your home, every year you owned it
optionLabels.principal_residence_some_years: Your home, but only some of the years
optionLabels.personal_use: A cottage or other property for your own use
optionLabels.flipped: A home owned less than 12 months, not sold because of a life event

propertyCost.ask: What you paid for it, with improvements
propertyCost.help: The adjusted cost base: the purchase price, the costs of buying, and the cost of improvements.

propertyOutlays.help: Real estate commission, legal fees and other costs of selling.

propertyYearsOwned.help: The tax years, from the year you bought it to 2025, counting both (Form T2091(IND), line 7).

propertyYearsDesignated.ask: Years it was your principal residence
propertyYearsDesignated.help: The years you designate it as your principal residence (Form T2091(IND), line 3). One more year is added for you.

hasRrspIncome.help: A T4RSP from each plan you took money out of in 2025.

hasBenefitsStatement.help: A T5007 from the board or the government that paid you.

hasRl5.help: An RL-5 from the Quebec government for social assistance or similar financial assistance, which also gives you a T5007.

hasFhsaWithdrawals.help: A T4FHSA from each FHSA you contributed to or withdrew from in 2025.

hasSupportReceived.help: Payments from a former spouse or partner under a court order or written agreement.

childSupportReceived.ask: The part that is child support
childSupportReceived.help: Child support under an order or agreement made after April 1997 isn't taxable.

rrspDeduction.help: Contributions from March 4, 2025 to March 2, 2026, up to your limit on last year's notice of assessment.

fhsaDeduction.help: Contributions in 2025 (box 18 of your T4FHSA), and any from earlier years you haven't deducted yet. You can also leave some for a later year.

hasWorkFromHome.help: Home-office expenses as an employee who worked from home more than half the time for at least 4 weeks in a row (Form T777). Your employer must sign Form T2200; keep it.

homeOfficeExpenses.help: Electricity, heat, water, home internet, maintenance and rent for your whole home. Mortgage interest and property tax don't count.

homeOfficeShare.help: The workspace's share of your home's area, times its share of the week's hours used for work. 12% of the area for 40 of 168 hours is 2.86%.

hasChildCare.help: Daycare, before- and after-school programs or day camps, so you or your spouse could work (Form T778). Enter them on one return of a couple; the app has the right spouse claim them.

childCareExpenses.help: Uploaded receipts are added; enter what isn't on one.

childCareDisabledUnder7.ask: Children born in 2019 or later with the disability tax credit

childCareDisabled7to16.ask: Children born from 2009 to 2018 with the disability tax credit

childCareDisabledOlder.ask: Children born in 2008 or earlier with the disability tax credit
childCareDisabledOlder.help: An infirm child who depends on you, of any age.

childCareInfirmOlder.ask: Children born in 2008 or earlier with an infirmity, without the disability tax credit
childCareInfirmOlder.help: An infirm child who depends on you.

childCareSpouseUnable.ask: Your spouse or partner couldn't care for the children for part of 2025
childCareSpouseUnable.help: They went to school, were confined for 2 weeks or more by an infirmity, or in prison, or you lived apart 90 days or more and reconciled (Form T778, Part C). Then you, with the higher net income, can claim part of the child care.

childCareSpouseWeeks.ask: Weeks they were a full-time student, infirm, in prison, or you lived apart
childCareSpouseWeeks.help: Form T778, Part C, situations b) to f).

childCareSpouseMonths.ask: Months they were a part-time student
childCareSpouseMonths.help: Form T778, Part C, situation a). Don't count a month with one of the weeks above.

hasMovingExpenses.help: A move at least 40 km closer to a new job or business (Form T1-M).

movingExpenses.help: Movers, travel, up to 15 days of temporary living, and the costs of selling your old home and buying the new one, less what your employer paid back.

movingIncome.ask: Income earned at the new location
movingIncome.help: Employment or self-employment income from the new job or business in 2025, less its deductions (union dues, CPP).

hasSupportPaid.help: Payments to a former spouse or partner under a court order or written agreement.

childSupportPaid.ask: The part that is child support
childSupportPaid.help: Child support under an order or agreement made after April 1997 isn't deductible.

carryingCharges.ask: Interest and fees to earn investment income
carryingCharges.help: Interest on money borrowed to invest (outside an RRSP or TFSA) and investment counsel fees.

hasDisabilitySupports.help: Attendant care, sign-language interpretation, devices and other supports paid so you could work or go to school (Form T929).

disabilitySupportsExpenses.help: Less what was paid back to you.

nonCapitalLosses.ask: Non-capital losses of earlier years to apply
nonCapitalLosses.help: Losses from a business or employment in earlier years that you haven't used yet.

netCapitalLosses.ask: Net capital losses of earlier years to apply
netCapitalLosses.help: From your notice of assessment. They can only reduce this year's taxable capital gains.

hasNorthernResidence.help: You lived in Yukon, the Northwest Territories or Nunavut for at least six months in a row, starting or ending in 2025. All three are a prescribed northern zone (Form T2222, northern residents deductions).

northernHome.ask: Others in your home claiming it
northernHome.help: The additional residency amount is only for the one person in a home who claims the basic residency amount.

optionLabels.alone: No one else in my home claims the northern residents deduction
optionLabels.shared: Someone else in my home claims it too

hasDisability.help: The CRA approved your Form T2201, Disability Tax Credit Certificate.

spouseInfirm.ask: Your spouse or partner depends on you because of an impairment
spouseInfirm.help: An impairment in physical or mental functions that makes them dependent on others for personal needs (Canada caregiver amount).

hasInfirmChildren.ask: A child under 18 with an impairment
hasInfirmChildren.help: A child who, because of an impairment, depends on others for personal needs much more than children of the same age.

hasInfirmDependant.ask: An adult relative with an impairment depends on you
hasInfirmDependant.help: A parent, grandparent, adult child, brother, sister, aunt, uncle, niece or nephew, 18 or older, with a net income under $28,798.

infirmDependantIncome.help: Line 23600 of their return, or what it would be.

infirmDependantHome.help: Some provinces give a larger caregiver amount for a dependant who lived in your home.

hasDisabledDependant.ask: A dependant with the disability tax credit
hasDisabledDependant.help: A child or another relative who depends on you, has no income and has an approved Form T2201.

disabledChildCare.ask: Child care and attendant care claimed for them
disabledChildCare.help: By you or anyone else, as child care or medical expenses.

hasVolunteerService.ask: Volunteer firefighter or search and rescue
hasVolunteerService.help: At least 200 hours of eligible volunteer service in 2025.

homeBuyers.help: Up to $10,000 when you or your spouse bought a first home in 2025, or a home for a person with a disability. A couple shares the $10,000.

homeAccessibility.help: Up to $20,000 to make a home safer or easier to use for someone 65 or older or with the disability tax credit.

studentLoanInterest.help: On loans under the Canada Student Loans Act or a provincial student loan program, for 2025 and up to five earlier years not claimed.

childTuitionTransfer.ask: Tuition transferred from a child or grandchild
childTuitionTransfer.help: The amount they designated to you on their T2202, up to $5,000 each.

childProvincialTuitionTransfer.ask: Provincial or territorial tuition transferred from a child or grandchild
childProvincialTuitionTransfer.help: The provincial or territorial amount they designated to you on their T2202. It can differ from the federal amount, since some provinces add education amounts.

hasOtherDependantMedical.help: An adult child or grandchild, a parent, grandparent, brother, sister, aunt, uncle, niece or nephew who depended on you.

politicalContributions.help: To a registered federal party, association or candidate, on official receipts.

provincialPoliticalContributions.help: To a registered party, association or candidate of your province or territory, on official receipts. In Quebec, to an authorized Quebec political party.

hasRentedHome.ask: Rented the home you lived in
hasRentedHome.help: A home you rented and lived in during 2025. Some provincial credits depend on the rent and on how many months you rented.

rentPaid.help: For the home you lived in, not counting any part a roommate or someone else paid.

rentMonths.help: Months of 2025 you rented and lived in it. Don't count months you paid rent to a relative, or for a campsite or a mobile home pad.

propertyTaxPaid.ask: Property tax paid on your home for 2025
propertyTaxPaid.help: Municipal and school taxes on the home you owned and lived in.

paidSchoolTaxes.ask: School taxes on a home you owned and lived in
paidSchoolTaxes.help: The school taxes on your 2025 property tax statement. A couple enters them on one return.

schoolTaxes.help: The gross school taxes, before the homeowners affordability tax credit advance was taken off.

schoolTaxAdvance.help: The advance taken off your property tax statement, or credited to your property tax account. 0 if none.

homeOwnedDays.ask: Days in 2025 you owned it and lived in it

publicTransitPaid.ask: Public transit paid as a senior
publicTransitPaid.help: Passes, tickets and fares for local public transit you used in 2025, at the senior fare where there is one, less any amount paid back to you. Ontario gives 15% of up to $3,000 if you were 65 or older on December 31, 2024.

teacherSupplies.ask: School supplies you paid as a teacher or early childhood educator
teacherSupplies.help: Up to $1,000 of supplies for your teaching, not paid back to you.

multigenerationalRenovation.help: Up to $50,000 to build a secondary unit for a senior or an adult with a disability to live with a relative (Schedule 12).

hasCwbAdvance.ask: Canada workers benefit paid in advance

hasRl19.ask: Quebec tax credits paid in advance (RL-19)
hasRl19.help: An RL-19 from Revenu Québec, for the work premium, childcare or home-support credits paid to you during 2025.

trainingCreditLimit.ask: Canada training credit limit from your 2024 notice of assessment
trainingCreditLimit.help: Half your 2025 tuition is refunded, up to this limit.

instalmentsPaid.help: Instalments you paid to the CRA for 2025.

hasTuition.ask: Tuition at a college or university
hasTuition.help: A T2202 from each school, for 2025.

hasRl8.ask: Tuition at a college or university in Quebec (RL-8)
hasRl8.help: An RL-8 from each school in Quebec, which also gives you a T2202.

unusedTuition.ask: Unused federal tuition from your 2024 notice of assessment

unusedProvincialTuition.ask: Unused provincial or territorial tuition from your 2024 notice of assessment
unusedProvincialTuition.help: The unused tuition and education amounts your notice shows for your province or territory, apart from the federal amount. If you lived in another one at the end of 2024, enter your unused federal amount. In Quebec, the unused tuition or examination fees on your 2024 notice of assessment from Revenu Québec (line 48 of Schedule T).

tuitionTransfer.ask: Tuition to transfer to your spouse or partner
tuitionTransfer.help: Up to $5,000 of this year's tuition, as designated on the back of your T2202.

medicalExpenses.help: For you, your spouse or your children. Uploaded receipts are added; enter what isn't on one. Either spouse can claim the family's medical expenses; it usually saves more on the lower income.

physicalActivityFees.ask: Physical activity fees to claim on this return
physicalActivityFees.help: Fees paid in 2025 to register you, your spouse or your children in a program of physical activity, or for membership in an eligible organization. In Newfoundland and Labrador your family can claim up to $2,000 in all; in Manitoba up to $500 for each person (you or your spouse under 25, each child under 18). Claim on one return or split between yours and your spouse's.

donations.help: On official receipts. Uploaded receipts and box 46 of your T4 are added; enter what isn't on one. Either spouse can claim both spouses' donations; claiming them together usually saves more.

childActivityFees.ask: Children's sports, arts and activity fees
childActivityFees.help: Registration or membership fees paid in 2025 for your children's sports, arts, cultural or recreational programs, less any reimbursement. For each child, count at most your province's limit ($300 in Saskatchewan, or $400 for a child with the disability tax credit; $500 in Nova Scotia and in Quebec, for a child born from 2009 to 2019; $1,000 in Prince Edward Island). A couple can split them; enter only what you claim on this return.

homeRenovationExpenses.help: Renovations to the home you own and live in, in Saskatchewan, paid from October 1, 2024 to December 31, 2025 (Schedule SK(S12)), such as a kitchen, bathroom, roof, floors, deck or furnace. Not repairs, maintenance, furniture or appliances. Enter the family's expenses on one return.

fertilityExpenses.help: Fertility treatment, fertility preservation or surrogacy costs paid in 2025, not covered by insurance, also entered with your medical expenses. Ontario, Saskatchewan and Yukon each have a credit for them, with their own rules on what counts. In Ontario and Saskatchewan only one spouse can claim it; in Yukon each spouse claims what they paid.

childFitnessFees.help: Fees you paid in 2025 for a program of physical activity for a child under 16, such as a sports team or a swimming class (Form YT479). Up to $1,000 for each child.

childArtsFees.ask: Children's arts and learning program fees
childArtsFees.help: Fees paid in 2025 for your children's arts, cultural, nature, learning or developmental programs, such as music or dance lessons, that aren't sports or physical activity, less any reimbursement. Count at most $500 for each child under 16. A couple can split them; enter only what you claim on this return.

qcLivedAlone.help: All of 2025 in a home you kept, alone or only with people under 18 or your children who were full-time students. It gives the amount for a person living alone (Schedule B) and counts for the solidarity tax credit (Schedule D).

hasRl31.help: An RL-31 from your landlord, for the solidarity tax credit (Schedule D). Copy its dwelling number (box A) onto Schedule D yourself; this app doesn't keep it.

qcHomeOwner.ask: Owned the home you lived in on December 31 (Quebec)
qcHomeOwner.help: For the solidarity tax credit (Schedule D). Copy the roll number from your municipal tax bill onto Schedule D yourself; this app doesn't keep it.

qcGroupDrugPlan.ask: Covered by a group drug insurance plan (Quebec)
qcGroupDrugPlan.help: Basic prescription drug insurance through a group plan at work, or through your spouse's or a parent's plan. Without one, you pay the premium of the public plan (Schedule K).

qcDrugMonthsJanJun.ask: Months from January to June it covered you
qcDrugMonthsJanJun.help: Count a month if the plan covered you for at least one day of it. 6 for all of them.

qcDrugMonthsJulDec.ask: Months from July to December it covered you

hasRl24.help: An RL-24 from each daycare or childcare provider, for the tax credit for childcare expenses (Schedule C).

qcChildCareReceipts.help: Childcare that qualifies for the Quebec credit, paid to a person who gave you a receipt instead of an RL-24. Not the reduced contribution of a subsidized daycare.

hasHomeSupport.help: Rent in an apartment building, or housekeeping, personal care, meal or nursing services you paid for, at 70 or older (Schedule J). A couple enters them on one return.

homeSupportRent.help: 0 if you lived in your own house or in a private seniors' residence. A seniors' residence (form TP-1029.61.MD-V) isn't handled.

homeSupportRentMonths.ask: Months you paid this rent in 2025

homeSupportServices.ask: Home-support services you paid, not in your rent
homeSupportServices.help: Housekeeping, grounds maintenance and snow removal, personal care, meal preparation and delivery, nursing.

qcChildTransfer.ask: Amount transferred to you by a child who is a student (Quebec)
qcChildTransfer.help: What your child, 18 or older and a full-time student with an RL-8, transfers to you on their Schedule S (lines 20.1 and 20.2).

qcChildTuitionTransfer.ask: Tuition credit transferred to you by a child (Quebec)
qcChildTuitionTransfer.help: The amount on line 68 of your child's Schedule T.

qcInstalmentsPaid.ask: Tax paid by instalments to Revenu Québec
qcInstalmentsPaid.help: Instalments you paid to Revenu Québec for 2025. Instalments paid to the CRA are a separate question.

spouseNetIncome.ask: Your spouse's or partner's 2025 net income
spouseNetIncome.help: Line 23600 of their return. Their return isn't prepared here, but some of your credits depend on it.

daysResident.ask: Days you lived in Canada in 2025
daysResident.help: From the day you arrived, or up to the day you left, counting that day. 365 if you lived here all year.

nonResidentIncome.ask: Your world income for the part of 2025 you didn't live in Canada
nonResidentIncome.help: All the income you had while you weren't a resident, from anywhere, in Canadian dollars. 0 if none.

nonResidentCanadianIncome.ask: The part of it from Canada
nonResidentCanadianIncome.help: Employment or business income from Canada in that period. If it is 90% or more of that world income, you can claim your full personal amounts.

departureProperty.ask: You left Canada owning shares, funds or other property
departureProperty.help: Only if you left Canada in 2025. Property other than Canadian real estate, a business in Canada, pensions and registered plans (RRSP, TFSA, FHSA) is treated as sold the day you left.

poolDonations.title: Claim both spouses' donations on one return
poolDonations.text: The first $200 of donations each year gets a lower credit. Claiming both spouses' donations on one return uses that lower rate once instead of twice. Your spouse's or partner's donations are then claimed on this return and left off theirs.
poolDonations.when: line.SPOUSES.together == 1 and spouse.line.OWN.donations > 0 and not answer.claimSpouseDonations

medicalOnOneReturn.title: Claim the family's medical expenses on this return
medicalOnOneReturn.text: Medical expenses count only above 3% of the claimant's net income (or $2,834, if less), so they usually save more on the return with the lower income. Your spouse's or partner's medical expenses are then claimed on this return and left off theirs.
medicalOnOneReturn.when: line.SPOUSES.together == 1 and spouse.line.OWN.medical > 0 and not answer.claimSpouseMedical
medicalOnOneReturn.amountLabel: Your spouse's or partner's medical expenses

tuitionTransfer.title: Transfer tuition you don't need to your spouse or partner
tuitionTransfer.text: You can transfer up to $5,000 of this year's tuition that this return doesn't use to your spouse or partner. Sign the transfer on the back of your T2202. The amount is saved as "Tuition to transfer to your spouse or partner" on Credits.

pensionSplit.title: Split your pension income with your spouse or partner
pensionSplit.text: You can move up to half of your eligible pension income to your spouse's or partner's return (Form T1032). With the lower income taxed there, the household usually pays less, and a spouse with no pension of their own can claim the pension income amount. The split brings your two net incomes as close as the limit allows. Both of you sign Form T1032 and attach it to both returns if you file on paper.
pensionSplit.when: line.SPOUSES.together == 1 and line.PEN.splitMax > 0 and answer.pensionSplit == 0 and spouse.answer.pensionSplit == 0 and line.T1.23600 > spouse.line.T1.23600

rrspNowOrLater.title: You can deduct your RRSP contributions in a later year
rrspNowOrLater.text: Your taxable income is in the lowest federal bracket. You don't have to deduct all your RRSP contributions for 2025: what you don't deduct carries forward, and may save more in a year when your income is higher. To deduct less, change the amount on Deductions.

fhsaNowOrLater.title: You can deduct your FHSA contributions in a later year
fhsaNowOrLater.text: Your taxable income is in the lowest federal bracket. FHSA contributions you don't deduct for 2025 carry forward with no time limit, and may save more in a year when your income is higher. To deduct less, change the amount on Deductions.

fhsaOverContribution.title: Your FHSA contributions may be over your participation room
fhsaOverContribution.text: Your FHSA participation room is $8,000 a year, plus at most $8,000 carried forward from last year, for contributions and RRSP transfers together. Your contributions and transfers for 2025 are more than $16,000. The CRA charges a tax of 1% a month on an excess FHSA amount until it is removed, on form RC727. This app doesn't prepare that form.

rrspOverContribution.title: Your RRSP contributions may be over your limit
rrspOverContribution.text: Your contributions are more than your RRSP deduction limit on your 2024 notice of assessment plus $2,000. The CRA charges a tax of 1% a month on the excess until it is withdrawn, on form T1-OVP. This app doesn't prepare that form. Check your limit, and the contributions you made after your notice of assessment.
rrspOverContribution.when: sum(NOA.box1) > 0 and sum(RRSP.box1) + sum(RRSP.box2) + sum(NOA.box2) > sum(NOA.box1) + param.rrspOverContributionAllowance

interestWithoutSlip.title: Interest is taxable even without a T5
interestWithoutSlip.text: A bank or credit union issues a T5 only when it pays you $50 or more. Interest under that is still income. If you earned any, enter it as a T5 on Income, from your account statements.
